situations: You carry a big wardrobe into a flat. The agent says the empty area inside the walls is large enough for it and for a bed too.
At work you ask whether the office has enough free space for two more desks.
You are in the kitchen, the bedroom and the bathroom of a new flat. Each one is a separate enclosed area with its own door. Which word fits?

en: to move, to move house, to relocate, to change, to get changed
situations: Your rent went up, so next month you will pack all your boxes and start living in a different flat.
You come home from work in a suit and put on jeans and a T-shirt instead.
Your company needs you in another city, so your whole family has to go and live there.
You use a ruler to measure a pencil. Each numbered mark on the ruler is one hundredth of a metre.
The tailor says your waist is 82 of these, a unit equal to ten millimetres.
A nurse measures how tall you are and says: one metre and seventy-two of what? Which unit, written 'cm', is meant?
You ask a waiter if you can sit at a table and he says nobody has booked it, so you can use it.
At the toilet door the lock shows green: nobody is inside.
It is Sunday and you have no work and no plans. Your schedule is empty all day.
From the hotel balcony you can see the mountains and the lake. What a beautiful ... from this window!
You quickly look at your phone for one second and then put it away again.
Your cat stares at you with a long, serious gaze while you eat your fish.

en: at the back, in the back
situations: The bus is full, so the driver tells you to walk to the end of the bus, behind everyone else.
In the cinema you sit in the very last row, far from the screen.
You look for the toilets in the restaurant and the waiter says they are at the rear of the room.
The teacher asks what you want to talk about in your presentation. You say it is about healthy food.
Your friends keep talking about football, but you want to change what the conversation is about.
You write an essay and the first line on the page says what it is about. Which word means 'topic'?
You see your neighbour's lights on at midnight and think quietly to yourself: why is he still awake?
You have not heard from your friend for weeks and you ask yourself what has happened. You do not ask anyone out loud.
After the exam you think silently: did I pass? Which verb describes this kind of silent questioning of yourself?
At home your family eats dinner around a piece of furniture with four legs and a flat top.
In the classroom you put your books and pens on the flat wooden surface in front of your chair.
In a restaurant the waiter says: 'I have reserved a place for four people. It is by the window.' What piece of furniture will you sit at?

en: herself, himself, itself, yourself, themselves, oneself
situations: Your little brother looks into the mirror and washes his own face. What word shows he does the action to himself?
Anna and Tom are in a hurry. Each of them quickly gets dressed, with no help from the other. Which small word goes with 'he' or 'she' for this?
A doctor says people should look after their own health. Which word shows the person does it for their own self, for he, she, it and they?

en: sight, attraction, point of interest, place of interest
situations: On your trip to Berlin you visit the old castle and the famous tower that every tourist wants to see.
At the tourist office you ask for a map with all the famous places worth visiting in town.
A friend asks what there is to do in Paris. You say the Eiffel Tower is the main one that visitors come to see.
At the station you buy a small piece of paper from the machine so you may ride the train to Munich.
The conductor walks through the carriage and asks every passenger to show what proves they paid for the journey.
You lose the paper you need for the bus to work and have to buy a new one. Which word means a travel ticket?

en: should, shall, to ought to, to be supposed to
situations: The doctor says you must take the medicine twice a day. It is what you are told to do.
Your mother says you ought to call your grandmother more often. What word fits 'I ... call her'?
The sign says the visitors are expected to leave their shoes at the door. Which verb expresses this duty or advice?
You buy a new shirt for a wedding, the colour of fresh snow and milk.
The doctor wears a coat the colour of fresh printer paper and the clouds on a sunny day.
You mix lots of light into your paint until it becomes the lightest possible colour, like a sheet of paper. Which colour word?
In March the snow melts, the flowers start to open and the birds come back. It is the season after winter.
You say your favourite time of year is when it gets warmer and the trees get new green leaves, just before summer.
A friend asks which season comes between winter and summer. Which word means 'spring'?
You heat a pan and pour a little golden liquid into it before you fry the eggs.
The car makes a loud noise. The mechanic says the engine needs a new liquid to lubricate its parts.
At the salad bar you take the green bottle made from olives and sprinkle some on your food.
You send your essay to the machine in the office so you can hold it on paper.
At the station you need a paper copy of your online booking, so you ask the clerk to put it on paper for you.
Your colleague needs the contract with ink on paper for the meeting in five minutes. Which verb describes making a paper copy from the computer?
You are on the phone and say to your friend: wait a very short time, I will be right back.
At a party someone asks you to stand still while she takes a picture at exactly the right instant.
A waiter says he will be with you in just a little while. Which word means a very short period of time?
You are walking in the mountains and your friend says: let's not stop here, let's keep going onwards.
The teacher stops the story at a good place. The children shout: tell us more, go on!
A sign shows that the train goes beyond this station to the next city. Which word means 'onwards' or 'further'?
On Saturday night you dance with friends to loud music and flashing lights.
Your sister is eighteen now, so she can go to the place where young people dance until 3 a.m.
A friend says: let's go out tonight, there is a good DJ at the place with the dance floor. What place?
In the playground a young female child with long hair is riding a swing.
A mother introduces her daughter, aged seven: this is my little ... Which word means a young female?
At the school party a boy and a young female pupil of ten years old are dancing together.
You see a coat in a shop window that costs 800 euros. You say you can't pay so much for it.
You have lunch near the tourist centre and the bill is very high for just a soup and a salad.
The price of a flat in the city centre is far more than most people can afford. Which adjective describes the cost?
You look out of the window and see grey clouds and water falling from the sky, so you take an umbrella.
The football match is cancelled because water is pouring down from the sky all afternoon.
A weather report says that tomorrow there will be drops falling from the clouds. Which verb describes this weather?
Every morning you stand at the stop and wait for a big yellow vehicle that takes people through the city.
Your school group is going on a trip. The driver opens the door of a large coach with forty seats.
At night the underground stops running, so you take the road vehicle that stops at every street corner.
You break a chocolate bar and give your friend one piece. Which word means one piece of a whole?
The mechanic says the car needs a new piece for the engine, but it is out of stock.
The teacher says the first section of the book is easy but the second section is harder.
You buy a pass online to see your favourite band play live on Friday night.
At the airport you show the boarding document on your phone so you can get on the plane.
You queue at the cinema box office and ask for two paper passes to the evening film.
Your bicycle has a flat tyre, so you get the tools out and make it work again.
The washing machine stopped working, so a technician comes to your flat to make it work again.
Your phone screen is cracked and you take it to a shop. What do they do to the phone?
You are in a paint shop and look at lots of little cards: red, blue, yellow and green. What is each one?
The teacher asks the children which shade they like best for their drawing: red, green or blue.
You want to repaint the kitchen walls, so you buy two big tins of liquid for the wall at the hardware store.
The teacher says: please open your books, every single one of you.
The waiter brings the bill and says that everything was perfect, the whole meal.
You enter a room and say hello to every single person in it. Which word means 'everyone' or 'everything'?

en: how, like, as, such as, what
situations: You meet a friend and ask about the way she is feeling and doing today.
You want to know the way to do something, like how to cook rice. Which question word do you start with?
You say that your sister is tall in the same way that your mother is tall. Which small word shows the comparison?
Every morning your neighbour walks his pet that barks and wags its tail around the park.
At the animal shelter a child asks to take home the friendly furry pet that barks, not the one that meows.
A sign at the shop door says that no pets that bark are allowed inside. What animal is it?
You arrive in a country where you don't know the language, the food or anyone. Everything feels very new and unknown.
A person you have never seen before knocks at your door. For you this person is a complete stranger.
A letter comes from someone you do not know, and the handwriting is unfamiliar. Which adjective describes something that is not familiar?
You are in the kitchen and your mother asks you to go to the cellar and bring a bottle of water.
The teacher asks you to go to the office and come back with the chalk.
Your child is playing outside. You go to the garden to bring him in for dinner.
On the back of the envelope there is a name and an address of the person who posted the letter.
You receive a parcel and wonder who sent it. You look at the label at the top left for the name of the person who posted it.
You fill in the post office form. One box asks for your name as the person who is posting the package, the other for the person who gets it.
At lunch you sit with a woman who works in the same office as you, and she tells you about her weekend.
You introduce Maria, who works next to you at the company, to your friend. Which word describes her?
Your female workmate is ill, so you offer to take over her tasks for the day.
Before work you buy a newspaper, a bar of chocolate and a bus ticket at the small stand on the street corner.
You are at the station and quickly need a bottle of water and some sweets from the small booth.
A friend asks where you buy magazines and lottery tickets. You point to a tiny shop with a window on the street.
On holiday in Rome you walk inside the old cathedral and look at everything with a guide.
The estate agent invites you to look at the flat you may want to rent. You go there to see it.
A school class goes to a factory to look around and see how cars are built.
It is December, there is snow on the ground and you wear a thick coat, gloves and a hat.
The three months with the shortest days: December, January and February.
In your country the coldest time of the year is coming. You can ski and the lakes freeze. Which season?
You peel a ripe banana and see its colour.
In the school bus, painted in a bright sunny colour, children go home.
A child draws the sun and chooses the crayon in the colour of a lemon.
Your wife, husband or the person you live with is the one you love and plan your life with.
In a business meeting you say that the other company is someone you work together with on the project.
For the dance class, the teacher says to choose the person who will dance with you. Which word means the person who is paired with you?
On Saturday morning you meet a friend in a small place to drink a cappuccino and eat a piece of cake.
You sit at a table outside, read a book and order a coffee from a waiter. Where are you?
Tourists in Vienna are tired and look for a cosy place that serves coffee and pastries.
You have been to Berlin one time, long ago, and it was beautiful. How many times?
The teacher says: do this exercise one time, then we will check. Which word means 'one time'?
Your grandmother says that in some future day we should all visit the sea together. Which adverb means 'some day'?

en: to excuse, to apologize, to apologise
situations: You step on a stranger's foot on the bus and say sorry, then you say that you regret what you did.
Your friend is late for the party. When he arrives he says sorry, asking you to forgive him.
You are late for a meeting because of traffic. You ask your boss to forgive you by saying that you are sorry.
For dinner your grandmother peels and boils round brown vegetables that grow underground, to eat with fish.
At the fast food restaurant you order the long golden fries; they are made from this vegetable.
You dig in the garden and find round vegetables growing under the soil, used for mashed dishes. Which vegetable?
At the station a voice from the loudspeaker says that the train to Hamburg is ten minutes late.
In the supermarket a voice over the speakers tells customers that the shop will close in fifteen minutes.
At the airport a speaker tells passengers to go to gate 12. Which word means this spoken notice over a loudspeaker?
You tell the taxi driver the spot where you want to be dropped off, the exact location.
You ask where the meeting will be held, and your boss names a small town near Munich.
On the form you write the name of the town where you were born, in the box for the birth place.
The old oak in the garden stopped growing and its leaves turned brown. The tree is slowly ceasing to live.
Your grandfather was very old and ill. One night he passed away peacefully.
The film's hero is shot at the end and his life ends. What verb describes this?
You drop your phone and the screen cracks into pieces. Now it does not work any more.
Your coffee machine will not switch on and nothing happens. It is out of order.
The chair leg snaps off when your uncle sits on it. What adjective describes the chair?
At the market you buy apples, oranges and bananas and put them in a bowl on the table.
The doctor tells you to eat more sweet things that grow on trees, and fewer cakes.
A shop has a section for apples, pears and grapes, next to the vegetable section. What is that section called?
You open your wallet and see that you do not have even one euro in it. Which word means 'not a single'?
At the shop the clerk says that there are no more tickets for tonight. Which word replaces 'a' in 'not a ticket'?
A friend asks if you have a car. You answer that you have not got one at all. Which word means 'not a'?
The week is almost over. After this working day the weekend starts, and you go out with friends in the evening.
The day between Thursday and Saturday is when many people finish work early.
Your boss says the project must be finished by the last working day of the week. Which day?

en: to get, to receive, to catch
situations: For your birthday you are happy to be given a new bike by your parents.
At the post office you are handed a parcel that you were waiting for. You obtain the package.
You run after the bus and manage to reach it just before the doors close; you catch it.
For breakfast you spread something yellow and creamy, made from milk, on your bread.
The recipe says to melt a hundred grams of the yellow dairy fat in the pan before adding the eggs.
At the supermarket you ask where to find the dairy product that goes on bread, next to the cheese.
The weather report says that tomorrow the temperature will be below zero, at three degrees below zero. Which word do you say before 'three'?
In a maths lesson the teacher says: ten take away four is six. Which word do you say for the subtraction sign?
Your bank account shows that you owe money. The number has a sign in front of it. Which word means 'negative'?
On Saturday you go to the supermarket and fill your trolley with bread, milk, vegetables and meat.
At the checkout, the cashier says that everything in your basket is for eating and drinking, so the tax is lower.
A charity collects tins, rice and pasta for people in need. What do they collect?
You invite all your friends to your flat to enjoy music, food and cake because it is your birthday.
At work the team has a small event in the kitchen with sparkling wine after a big success.
The family gets together on New Year's Eve with fireworks and drinks. Which word describes this kind of party or event?
A stranger helps you carry your heavy bags upstairs, and you tell him you are very grateful.
After the nice dinner, your friend gives you a gift. You smile and say how grateful you are, giving her your thanks.
The teacher helped you with the exam. You want to show gratitude. Which verb means to express thanks?
Your little niece gives you a hug and a drawing. She is such a sweet, gentle girl.
You begin a letter to a person you like very much: 'Hello, my ... Anna'. Which word fits before her name?
A neighbour brings you soup when you are ill. You tell her she is very kind and nice.
The bus is full, and many men, women and children are standing there. You say that a lot of persons are inside.
At the concert there are thousands of persons in the crowd, all singing.
A friend says that some persons in town are unfriendly. Which word means many persons in general?
You go to a German shop and give the cashier a coin. The currency is used in Germany, France and Italy.
A coffee costs three of them. What currency do you pay with in Berlin?
You travel from Poland to Germany and exchange your money into the currency used there, which has the sign €.
In the morning you eat bread with jam and drink coffee before you leave for work.
At the hotel you go to the dining room at eight o'clock where there are rolls, cheese and eggs. What meal is that?
Which meal comes first in the day, before lunch and dinner?
You write an email to your teacher and press the button so it goes to her inbox.
You put a birthday card in an envelope and post it to your grandmother in another country.
Your boss asks you to forward the documents to the client by courier. Which verb means to make something go to another person?
You open your wardrobe and see trousers, shirts, dresses and jackets. What do you wear on your body every day?
At the second-hand shop you donate the things you no longer wear, such as shirts and skirts.
At the airport you pack T-shirts and trousers into your suitcase. What are you packing?
At the doctor you step onto the scale and the nurse writes how heavy you are: seventy kilos.
At the post office the clerk puts your parcel on the scale to check how heavy it is, to know the cost.
The plane only allows bags that are twenty kilos at most. What does this limit refer to?
The teacher says to the student at the back: please come to the front of the class, move up.
In a queue the person behind you says that you can go ahead, to the front of the line.
The bus driver says: move up in the bus, there is space in the front. Which small word means 'forwards'?
Your village is 200 kilometres away from the city, a long distance from here. Which adjective describes this?
You buy trousers that fit loosely and are not tight at all. They are very roomy.
The river is very broad, so it takes a long time to swim across it.
A friend tells you that it will rain tomorrow. You say that you think so, too, or you accept it as true.
A child says the story is true and he trusts what his father said. He accepts it.
You are not sure if the shop is open. You say that you suppose it is, because it is a weekday.
The postman needs to know the street, house number and city so he can deliver the letter to your home.
You fill in a form and write your street name, number and postcode in the box. What is that information called?
The taxi driver asks where to take you. You give him the name of the street and number of your house.
You point at a man and say: that is the man who lives next door. Which small word means 'who'?
The teacher puts three small words in front of nouns, masculine, feminine and neuter, as the definite articles. Which words are they?
You say about a car: 'the car which I bought is red'. Which word means 'which'?
You borrow a small writing instrument with ink inside and a click button from the shop to sign the form.
The teacher says you can use pencil or a blue one with a ball tip for your test.
A colleague lends you the small blue writing tool in his pocket to write the phone number. What is it? A short, informal word.
At a Bavarian garden you order a cold glass of golden drink with white foam, made from hops and barley.
On Saturday evening your friends watch football and drink bottles of a drink with 5% alcohol, made from malt.
In Germany people say it is the most famous drink at Oktoberfest, drunk from a big glass mug.
On the phone the clerk can't understand your surname, so you say each letter one by one.
At the hotel reception you say your name letter by letter, M-U-E-L-L-E-R, so the clerk can write it down.
The teacher asks you to say the word out loud, one letter at a time. What is that action?
On Mother's Day you give flowers to the woman who gave birth to you.
A child calls out for the woman who cooks his dinner and puts him to bed. Who is she?
You introduce the woman next to you to your friends: she is my female parent.
At the airport the officer checks whether your passport is still not expired.
The bus ticket can be used until midnight and is accepted by the driver. It is still ...
You show the clerk a coupon, but it ran out last month, so it is no longer accepted. What word did the clerk say before 'no longer'?
It is the hottest month of the year, schools are closed and you go swimming at the lake. It is the seventh month.
You have your birthday between June and August. Which month is it?
Which month comes after June and before August?
The lottery prize is a one followed by six zeros in euros. Which number is that?
A big city has 1,000,000 inhabitants. How many is that?
Your uncle says that it would cost a thousand times a thousand euros to buy that villa.
You try on a red jacket in a shop and smile. You say that it is nice for you, you find it pleasant.
Your friend asks how the film was. You say that it was enjoyable for you, in the sense that it pleased you.
The tourists say that the city is very pleasant to them. Which verb means that something is pleasing to someone?
In the maths lesson the teacher says: two ... three is five. Which word do you say for the addition sign?
The weather forecast says that tomorrow it will be above zero, at five degrees. Which word could you say before 'five' for a positive temperature?
The shop clerk adds the delivery fee to the price. Which small word shows the addition sign?
At a wedding the bride puts on a ring and becomes the female spouse of her husband.
A man introduces the woman next to him, who he married two years ago.
On the form, in the family status section, you write the woman married to the applicant. Which word?
At 8 a.m. the children carry their bags to the building where they have lessons from teachers.
After the summer holidays the building is open again and pupils learn maths and reading there.
Your six-year-old daughter starts at a place where she will learn to read and write.
You get a new job, so you open a bottle of sparkling wine with your friends to mark the great news.
It is your birthday and you invite friends to enjoy music, food and cake together.
On New Year's Eve everyone is dancing and having fun at midnight. Which verb describes this?
On this day most shops are closed and many people rest at home or go to church.
The day between Saturday and Monday is the day when the weekend ends.
Your friend asks which day closes the week, right before Monday starts.
On a form there are two boxes, one for female and one for the other gender. You tick the box for a man.
A zoo guide says that the lion with the big mane is a masculine animal, not a lioness.
The doctor asks about the gender of the patient: it is a man, so he writes down the word for 'masculine'.
On the board at the airport you see that the plane to Madrid leaves at 10:45. What is the information about?
Your plane takes off in two hours, so you must hurry through security.
Your friend asks what time your flight leaves the ground. Which noun means the time when the plane starts?
You forget your friend's birthday and send her a message saying you are sorry. This is a way of saying sorry.
The student comes late and tells the teacher a reason why he was not on time, for example that the bus broke down.
After you push a person in the shop, you say 'Sorry!' What noun means this expression of regret?

en: to find, to think, to locate, to discover
situations: You look for your keys everywhere and finally see them under the sofa. You come across them.
A friend asks your opinion about the new film. You say that you think it is great.
You search the internet for a restaurant nearby and discover a good Italian one.
Your grandmother does not use email. She writes by hand on paper, puts it in an envelope with a stamp and posts it.
The postman puts a paper message in an envelope with your name in your mailbox.
You write to the town office to ask a question. You use a sheet of paper and a stamp. Which word means this kind of written message?
You talk about your brother, who is at the door: 'Where is Peter? ... is at the door.' Which small word means 'he'?
You point to the dog and say that this animal is hungry. Which word for the male animal can also mean 'it' for a masculine noun?
Your friend asks about the new teacher. You answer that the man is very nice. Which pronoun replaces 'the man'?
Every summer you stay with your mother's parents and your father's parents in the countryside.
At Christmas the whole family sits at the table: parents, children and the older generation, the parents of your parents.
A child draws a picture of the grandmother and grandfather together. What is the word for both of them?
You say first you will cook dinner, afterwards you will watch TV. Which word means 'afterwards'?
The teacher says: first read the text, next write the answers. Which small word connects the second step?
A friend asks: if you don't come, what will we do next, at that point? Which word means 'in that case' or 'at that time'?
In your bedroom you hang your shirts and jackets in a tall piece of furniture with doors.
In the kitchen you keep plates and glasses in a piece of furniture on the wall with shelves behind doors.
The moving men carry a big wooden piece of furniture with doors and shelves up the stairs.
The teacher asks what you will be doing in the weekend. You say you will be making a cake and doing your homework.
You ask your sister what she is doing right now, because you see her working at the table.
A friend asks you to prepare a coffee for him. Which common verb means 'to do' or 'to make'?
The race car passes the others at 300 kilometres per hour. It moves at great speed.
You need to finish your homework within five minutes, so you work at a high pace.
A friend says the express train takes only two hours from Berlin to Munich. Which adjective describes the train?
At the butcher's you buy beef and pork, and a vegetarian friend says that she does not eat this.
The recipe says: put the pieces of chicken, lamb or beef into the pan.
A hungry man is choosing from the menu between a dish with fish and a dish with pork. Which food word covers beef, pork and lamb?
After work you go to the gym, run or play football. What kind of activity is this?
At school there are lessons where pupils play volleyball and run. Which school subject is that?
Your doctor says that regular physical activity such as swimming and cycling is good for your heart.
For dinner you stand in the kitchen and prepare pasta and sauce on the stove.
You put the eggs in a pot of water on the stove and wait ten minutes until they are hard.
Your father loves to prepare meals for the whole family on Sundays. Which verb means this activity?
In the evening the sun goes down in one direction. At the compass this is the opposite of east.
Your friend lives in France, which is in the direction left of Germany on the map. Which compass direction is that?
On the compass there are four directions: north, south, east and ... Which one is missing, the one where the sun sets?
The doctor says to take care, because staying healthy is important for the whole span between birth and death.
Your grandfather tells stories about his time on Earth, from his childhood until now.
A poster says: enjoy every day of your existence. Which noun means what we live from birth to death?
In July you wear shorts, go swimming and eat ice cream because the sun is hot.
The season with the longest days and the school holidays comes after spring.
A friend asks which season is the warmest. Which season is it, between spring and autumn?
In a race you cross the finish line after everyone else; you are behind all of the others. Which adjective describes your place?
The bus driver says that the final bus of the evening leaves at midnight. Which adjective do you use?
The teacher says this is the end of the book, the page that comes after all the others. Which adjective means 'final'?
Your boss asks you to explain the plan in just a few words, not a long speech.
You tell a neighbour at the door that you will talk to her for only a minute, because you are in a hurry.
The phone rings during dinner. You say you will be back in a moment. Which adverb means 'for a short time' or 'in a few words'?

en: to understand, to comprehend, to apprehend
situations: The teacher explains the grammar twice and now you finally get the meaning. You say: ah, I see what it means now.
A tourist speaks very fast on the phone and you cannot follow what she says. You do not grasp it at all.
Your friend tells a joke in another language. You laugh because you got the point.
At the fast food counter you order a paper bag of long golden potato sticks with ketchup.
Children at the pool bar ask for hot, salty sticks of fried potato to eat with their burger.
The waiter asks what side dish you want with your sausage, potato salad or the fried potato sticks.
At the train station you ask the clerk for facts about the departure time of the next train.
You read a website to learn facts about the opening times of the museum.
A leaflet gives you all the details you need about the hotel. What do you call these facts and details?
On holiday you hold up your phone and click to capture your family in front of the beach.
Your grandmother has an old black-and-white image of herself as a girl, in a frame on the wall.
You send your friend the image from the party. What do you call this picture taken by a camera?
You say to your wife that she is the most important person in your life and that you have deep feelings for her.
A mother tells her baby, with a gentle voice, that she has very strong feelings of affection for him.
In a song the singer says that he has deep feelings for a girl. Which verb is this, stronger than 'to like'?
The teacher says that all students, one by one, will get a book. She means each single person.
At the party, one by one, each guest gets a little gift.
The sign says that any person who enters must wear a helmet. Which word means each, one at a time?
It is midnight, there is no bus any more, so you phone for a car with a driver and a light on the roof to take you home.
At the airport you stand in the queue outside to ride in a yellow car and pay by the kilometre.
Your friend is drunk, so you call for a car with a meter that will take him to his flat.
Your friend tells a story about his cat and everybody laughs out loud for ten minutes.
At the party the guests are in a good mood and enjoy themselves, laughing and dancing.
A film about two clowns makes children laugh a lot. Which adjective describes the film?
At school a man stands in front of the class and explains maths to the pupils.
A man in your language course corrects your homework with a red pen and gives you marks.
Your son says that the man who teaches him German is very strict. Who is he?

en: to be able to, to can
situations: You tell the teacher that you know how to swim and are able to do it for 500 metres.
A friend asks if you are capable of speaking German. You say yes, a little.
The boss asks whether it is possible for you to come early tomorrow. Which verb expresses ability or possibility?
The recipe says to add 250 of these of flour. It is a thousandth of a kilo.
At the post office the letter weighs only twenty of these.
At the market the seller weighs a hundred of cheese on the scale. Which small unit of weight is it?
You hand something to your friend and say: it is in this place where I am standing, right at this spot.
At the school the teacher takes attendance. A pupil raises his hand and says: I am present in this place.
A tourist asks where the museum is, and you point to the ground and say it is in this very spot. Which adverb means 'in this place'?
You call your friend but nobody picks up. A machine records your voice and plays it later.

You meet a new person at the party and ask about his home country. Which question word?
A friend gives you a nice cake and you ask: where is it from? Which question word?
The teacher asks the student: from which country do you come? Which question word?
On Father's Day the children give a present to the man who raised them.
A child calls out for the man who gets him from school every day, his male parent.
You introduce the man next to you as the husband of your mother. He is a male parent. Who?

en: to give away, to hand in, to submit, to deliver, to dispense
situations: At the end of the exam you give your paper to the teacher, so that she can check it.
At the reception you leave your coat with the clerk, who takes it for the evening.
You hand in the form at the office before Friday. Which verb means to hand in?
In the evening you sit on a soft piece of furniture in the living room with cushions and watch TV.
A guest stays overnight and sleeps on the soft piece of furniture in the living room.
The cat sleeps on the soft seat for several people, in front of the television.
The host opens the door and says that you are received with joy and invites you in.
A sign at the airport says that the visitors are greeted warmly. Which adjective?
The family is happy when the guests arrive. They say: you are very ... here.
You have a pain in your back, so you make an appointment at the place where your doctor treats patients.
The sign on the door says that the surgery is open from 8 to 12.
The company wants an employee with experience in actually doing the work, not only from books. What do you call this kind of experience?
At the hotel the clerk says to a man: how can I help you? She uses a polite title for him.
On the envelope you write a polite title before the family name of a man.
At the beginning of a formal letter you write: Dear ... Müller. Which word is used for a man?
The waiter brings the bill and you take your wallet to give the amount in cash.
You buy a coffee and give the cashier two euros.
At the end of the month you hand over the rent to your landlord. What do you do with the money?
After school he spent five years at university, learning medicine, and then he became a doctor.
Your sister will begin her time at the university in October.
At the application form the question is about the time you spent at university. What noun?
You give a book to your brother. You say: I give a book to ... Which word is used for 'him' as an indirect object?
You ask about your friend and say: I phone ... every day. Which pronoun means 'him' as the indirect object?
The teacher says that you should help the new pupil, and say: help ... with the homework. Which word?
You meet a business partner and put out the part of your body at the end of your arm to say hello.
The child holds his mother's part of the body with five fingers when they cross the street.
The doctor looks at the part of your body with five fingers, because you cut it with a knife.

en: so, (like) that, this way, as, such
situations: You show your child how to tie shoes: do it in this way. Which small word means 'in this way'?
A friend asks if the film was good and you say that it was extremely good. Which word means 'such' or 'that much'?
The teacher says: write the letter like this, and shows an example. Which small word?
You look at the lake, the mountains and the flowers and say that it is very pleasing to the eye.
The weather is sunny and warm. You say that it is pleasant today.
A friend shows you her new dress and you say that it looks lovely. Which adjective?
The car does not work, so the mechanic says that he will fix it and the work will cost 200 euros.
The sign in the window says: we do the work of mending your phone, in one hour.
The washing machine has stopped, so you call a technician to do the job of making it work again. What noun?

en: to pick up, to collect, to fetch, to get
situations: After school the mother stands at the gate and takes her child home.
The parcel is at the post office and you walk there to take it with you.
A friend says that he will come to your house at 7 o'clock with his car and take you to the party.
A sign on the road says: be careful, the surface is wet. What is the single word at the top?
At the station a voice says that you must stand back from the edge of the platform, with a warning word first.
You show your respect for an old person, giving him the regard that he deserves. Which noun?
You put milk, cheese and butter into a big cold box in the kitchen so that they stay fresh.
The ice cream melts, because you left it on the table instead of putting it in the cold place in the kitchen.
At the shop you buy an electric machine, which keeps food cold, together with a freezer.

en: to phone, to telephone, to make a phone call
situations: Every evening you sit on the sofa and speak to your mother over the line for an hour.
The boss says that he is in a conversation on the phone and cannot be disturbed right now.
You call your friend in another country with your mobile. What is the action?
The shoes are too small and the part of your body at the end of your leg hurts.
The dancer stands on the tips of the parts of her body that are in her shoes.
The doctor asks you to step on the scale with the parts of your body at the bottom of the legs. What is it?
In autumn the air moves strongly, and the leaves fly around, and your hat flies away.
On the beach the sailors are happy, because the air moves and fills the sails.
The weather report says that tomorrow there will be strong moving air from the west. What noun?
The test is not difficult at all. Everybody finishes it in ten minutes.
The bag weighs only two kilos. It is not heavy and you can carry it with one hand.
The jacket is thin and weighs almost nothing. Which adjective describes its weight?
After the help of your neighbour you say: many thanks. What noun expresses what you feel?
At the end of the speech the president expresses his gratitude to all the people who helped.
A card says: with deep gratitude for your help. What noun is it?
The boy was small last year and next year he will be tall. What does he do with respect to size?
You say that tomorrow you will go to the cinema. Which verb expresses the future?
It is cold in the morning, but in the afternoon it will get warm. Which verb describes the change?
On the screen at the airport you see the time when the plane from Rome lands. What is the information?
Your friend phones to say that she will be there at 5 o'clock, when the train reaches the station.
At the train station a sign says 'Arrivals and Departures'. What is the opposite of departure?
The boss says that you must come to his office this very second, without waiting. Which adverb?
The doctor says that you should take the medicine without delay, at once.
You call the taxi and the driver says that he will be there straight away. Which adverb?
You look at the wall in the kitchen to see that it is already 8 o'clock.
Your grandfather gives you a small device that you wear on your wrist to show the time.
The train leaves at 9 ... Which word means 'o'clock', or also the instrument that shows the time?
At the bank, you write your name on the form with a writing tool with a small ball at the tip and blue ink.
You buy a small plastic writing instrument with a clicking button in the stationery shop.
The teacher says that tests must not be written with a pencil but with a blue writing instrument. What is it?

en: to answer, to reply, to respond
situations: The teacher asks a question and you give your reply in a loud voice.
You receive an email from your boss, and write back the same day.
A friend asks if you are coming to the party. You say: yes. What did you do?
Before email, the office used a machine to send paper copies over the phone line.
The lawyer asks you to send the contract by a machine that scans the paper and sends it over a telephone line.
The old office has a printer, a telephone and a machine for sending documents over the phone line.
You show a photo and say that this is the car that belongs to you. Which word means 'belonging to me'?
You introduce a person: this is the sister who belongs to me. Which possessive word?
At the airport the officer asks whose bag it is. You say: it belongs to me. Which word means 'my' or 'mine'?
At night the baby is sleeping, so you speak with a soft voice and walk without noise.
In the library the librarian asks everybody not to talk loudly. Which adjective?
The new electric car makes almost no sound. Which adjective describes it?
At the entrance of the cinema there is a queue of people who wait to get in.
You look for the door where you can come into the building, and the sign says: use the door at the side.
The letter of the bank arrives on Monday. The date of its arrival is written down as receipt.

en: to take care of, to look after, be concerned
situations: Your neighbour is on holiday, so you give water to her plants and feed her cat. You take responsibility.
The mother looks after her sick child and gives him medicine.
The teacher says that you must arrange the project yourself. Which verb means to take care of something?
In the hotel you get the key for a place with a bed, a window and a bathroom, number 305.
The flat has a kitchen, a bathroom and three of these: a living room and two bedrooms.
A student rents a place with a bed and a desk in a shared flat. What do you call each space?
The teacher says that your desk is a mess, and that you must put everything in the right place. What is it?
Your mother looks into your room and is happy: everything is clean and in its place.
In the rules for the library, the books must be in the sequence of the alphabet. What is it called?
The runner crosses the finish line at high speed. Which adverb describes how he runs?
The teacher says: please answer in a short time, do not wait. Which adverb?
A friend says: come soon, we do not have much time. Which adverb describes the way you should come?
You hear that your friend has passed the exam and you say 'well done' with a smile.
On your birthday you receive many cards and messages with kind words about your day.
After the wedding, the guests tell the bride and the groom that they are happy for them. What noun?

en: to shine, to seem, to appear
situations: After the rain the sun comes out and gives light and warmth to the garden.
The man looks very tired. You say that he gives the impression of not having slept.
The text says that the shop is closed, although the light is on. Which verb means 'to give the impression'?
The young mother carries a very small child who is only three months old and sleeps all day.
At the hospital the nurse brings the newborn to the mother.
A couple buys a small bed, tiny clothes and a pram, because their child will soon be born.
The man with white hair and a stick is eighty years of age. He is not young.
The church in the town centre was built in the year 1200. It is not new.
You do not buy the car because it has been used for twenty years and looks worn. Which adjective?
After a big meal you feel full, and the front part of your body below the chest is round and hurts.
The doctor says that you have a pain in the part of the body where the stomach is.
The child says that he has pain in his tummy. Which part of the body?
At the station the voice says that the train to Hamburg will leave from number 7, where you wait on the platform.
The train drives on steel lines in the ground. What are these lines called?
At the station the sign says: do not cross the lines. What are they?
A friend phones you and asks if you will visit him this evening. You say: yes, I will be there at 8 o'clock.
The train arrives at the station at 10:15. What does it do?
The teacher says to a pupil outside: please enter the room. Which verb describes coming towards the speaker?
In the supermarket there is a sign with a special price for tomatoes this week.
The shop clerk says that the shop has a large selection of jackets in different sizes.
A company writes to you and says that it will do the work for 500 euros. What do you call this written price proposal?
After school she goes to live in France, Spain and Italy, in other countries than hers.
The company sends its employees to work in a country that is not their home country. Where do they go?
A friend says: I will go on holiday not in my own country but somewhere else, on the other side of the border.

en: to fill out, to fill in, to complete, to satisfy, to take up
situations: At the bank the clerk gives you a paper with empty boxes, and you write your name and address into them.
At the doctor's reception you must write information in the boxes of the paper.
The teacher says that you should put the missing words into the gaps of the sentence.
After the exam the teacher tells you your mark. What is it?
The football match is over, and the newspaper says 2:1. What do you call this?
The doctor tells you the outcome of the blood test on the phone. What noun?
The road runs for ten kilometres without any curve. It is not curved at all.
You draw a line with a ruler on the paper. It is not bent. Which adjective?
The number 4 is not odd, but ... Which adjective describes numbers like 2, 4 and 6?
You ask your friend if he has plans for this day, not tomorrow. Which adverb?
The teacher says that the test will be written on this day, not on another day.
Nowadays most people have a mobile phone. In contrast with the past, what adverb means 'at the present time'?
On December 25th, all shops are closed and most people do not work. What kind of day is it?
On the first of January nobody goes to the office, because it is a day off for everybody in the country.
On the calendar some days are marked in red, such as Christmas and Easter. What are these days?
You meet a friend and ask how he is. Which word means 'you' for a close friend, a child or a family member?
A boy says to his sister: are you coming with me to the shop? Which pronoun is used for 'you' in the informal form?
Two students who are friends talk to each other: what pronoun means 'you' for one person informally?
A road sign says the next town is 5 of these away. Each one is 1,000 meters. What is this unit of distance called?
You go jogging. After one hour your watch shows you ran 10 of them, which is 10,000 meters.
You drive to the airport and the sign says 'Airport 25'. Which word means 'kilometre'?

en: to rent, to hire, to lease
situations: You have no car, so you pay a company a small amount for two days to use one for a trip. What do you do with the car?
You are a student. Every month you pay the owner money to live in a small flat that is not yours.
On holiday you pay a shop to use a bicycle for the afternoon and bring it back in the evening. Which word means 'to rent'?
At a family dinner your brother and your sister sit next to you. What do you call the three of you together, as children of the same parents?
A form asks how many of these you have. You write: one older sister and two younger brothers.
A friend says: 'I am an only child.' You answer that you have a brother and a sister. What is the plural word for brothers and sisters together?
You move into a new flat. It is empty, so you go to a big shop to buy a table, chairs, a sofa and a bed.
Two men from the moving company carry your wardrobe, desk and shelves up the stairs.
Your living room looks bare because it has no sofa, no table and no shelves. Which word means 'furniture'?
You buy a car in a shop. The label says it was built in Germany, France or Spain, so it comes from the continent with Paris and Rome.
On TV, clubs from Madrid, Munich and Paris play in a cup for teams from this continent. Which adjective fits this cup?
At a customs office, one line is for people with a passport from countries of this continent, and another line is for people from everywhere else.
You ask your neighbour if he can water your plants while you are away. What is such a polite question for help called?
Your boss says: 'I have one small thing to ask of you.' You listen. What is the noun for what she wants to ask?
A child writes a note to her mother: 'Mum, I have something I want to ask you.' Which noun means 'a request'?

en: to watch television, to watch TV
situations: After dinner you sit on the sofa and look at a film on the screen in the living room.
It is raining, so you stay at home all evening and follow the news and a quiz show on the box.
Your friend calls and asks what you are doing. You say you are sitting at home and looking at programs. Which verb means 'to watch TV'?
You have a fever and a sore throat. You make an appointment with a man in a white coat who examines you and writes a prescription.
A friend says: 'My uncle works at the hospital and treats sick people.' Which word is used for a male medical person like him?
Your child falls and hurts his arm. You call the emergency number and ask for a man who can treat him. Which word means 'doctor' (male)?
Today is Wednesday. You tell your colleague that you went to the cinema on Tuesday evening.
You see a friend and say: 'Sorry I did not call. I was very busy the whole day before today.'
Which word means 'yesterday', the day before today?
Your dentist appointment is at 10 o'clock, after breakfast but long before lunch. At what part of the day is it?
At school the lessons begin at 8 and a long break comes at 11. The part of the day before noon is nearly over.
A shop sign says: 'Open from 9 to 12, then closed.' Which noun means the time from about 9 to noon?

en: to barbecue, to have a barbecue, to grill
situations: It is a sunny Saturday. You and your friends stand in the garden and cook sausages and steaks over hot charcoal.
At a summer party in the park, somebody brings meat and vegetables to cook on a metal rack over a fire.
Your neighbour invites you to come on Sunday for food outside on his barbecue. Which verb means 'to barbecue'?
You cut a pizza into four equal pieces and eat one of them.
You live in a lively part of the city with many cafes and old houses. People call such a part of a city by this name.
A friend says: 'I only need one of four equal parts of the cake.' Which noun means 'quarter'?
At the airport the officer asks for a small card with your photo, name and date of birth.
At the entrance of the company building you wear a card on a band around your neck so the guard can see who you are.
You want to buy a train ticket with a student discount. The clerk says you must show your student card. Which word means 'ID card'?
You cut an apple into two equal pieces and give one piece to your friend.
A shop has a sale: you pay only 50 percent of the normal price for a jacket.
The bottle was full yesterday. Today only 50 percent of the water is left. Which adjective describes this bottle?
For breakfast you put cheese and thin slices of pink meat from a pig on your bread roll.
At the butcher's counter you ask for 200 grams of smoked pork, thinly sliced, for your sandwiches.
A pizza has tomatoes, cheese and slices of pig meat on it. Which word means 'ham'?
Your football team scores three goals and the other team scores one. Your team gets the points.
You buy a lottery ticket and the numbers on it are the right ones, so you get a big prize.
You play chess against your uncle and for the first time you are better than him. Which verb means 'to win'?
In a shop you ask for the jacket in a larger one, because 'M' is too small. What are you asking about?
A doctor measures you and says: 'You are 1.80 meters.' Which noun describes how tall you are?
Your new flat is nice, but the living room is not big enough for a large sofa. What do you worry about?
You see a strange object on the table and you do not know it. You point at it. Which word do you use to ask 'What is that?'
You did not hear your friend clearly. You ask him to repeat by asking about the thing he said. Which question word means 'what'?
Your friend holds a gift behind his back. You are curious about the thing inside. Which word do you use to ask 'What is it?'
On a form at the doctor's office there is a line for the number that shows in which year you were born, for example 1995.
You say: 'I am 30 years old.' The clerk asks you to write the number of the year you first came into the world.
Your teacher wants to know when you were born. She asks only for the number of the year, not the day or the month. Which word means 'year of birth'?
On Sunday your family goes by bus to a lake for the whole day and brings sandwiches.
Your school class leaves the classroom for a day and goes to visit a castle together with the teacher.
A friend asks what you did last weekend. You say: 'We took a short day journey to the mountains.' Which noun means 'excursion'?

en: in former times, in the past, early
situations: Your grandfather says: 'Long ago there was only one small shop in our village, but now there are three supermarkets.'
You look at an old photo and say: 'I had long hair in the time before now.' Which word means 'in the past'?
You always get to work at 7:30. Today your boss asks you to be there at 6, earlier than normal. Which word means 'earlier'?

en: to depart, to fly away, to take off
situations: You stand at the airport. Your plane leaves the ground at 14:20 and you wave goodbye to your friends.
The departure board says your flight to Berlin goes up into the air at 8:10 tomorrow morning.
A colleague asks: 'When does your plane leave?' You answer: 'At six o'clock.' Which verb means 'to fly away, to take off'?
At the market you buy a fruit that is green or yellow, round at the bottom and thin at the top. It is not an apple.
For dessert your grandmother serves a sweet fruit with a long shape, cut in two, with chocolate sauce.
You are in a fruit shop. You ask for apples, bananas and one more fruit shaped like a drop. Which word means 'pear'?
You try to carry a suitcase full of books up the stairs, and your arms hurt because it weighs a lot.
In the exam you cannot solve most questions because they are very hard to understand.
A friend says: 'The test was not easy at all.' Which adjective can mean both 'heavy' and 'difficult'?
At the post office you wait in line until the clerk behind the window can help you.
It is dark in your room. You press a small button on the wall and the lamp turns on. What do you press?
At the train station you go to a window to buy a ticket. Which noun means 'counter' or 'switch'?
A girl studies biology at the university. She goes to lectures and writes exams. How do you call her?
You meet a woman in the library. She says she is learning for her law exam at the university. Which word describes her?
On the bus, a young woman shows a card and gets a cheaper ticket because she is still at university. Which word means 'student' (female)?

en: to put (vertically), to place, to position, to set, to provide
situations: You take a bottle from the shelf and put it upright on the table, next to the glass.
The waiter brings the cake and puts it in front of you on the table. He does not lay it down flat.
Your friend helps you in the kitchen. You tell her to put the pots upright in the cupboard. Which verb means 'to put, to place (upright)'?
Every morning you go to the bakery and buy a small round piece of bread, not a big loaf, for your breakfast.
At the hotel breakfast buffet you cut a small crispy piece of bread in half and put butter and cheese on it.
At the bakery you say: 'I would like two of the small ones, please.' Which word means 'bread roll'?
Your teacher says: 'Please write ten sentences for the next lesson.' You must do it at home in the afternoon.
Your child says he cannot play outside yet because he must finish his maths exercises for school first.
After school your friend asks if you want to go to the cinema. You say you cannot because you still have school work to do at home. Which word means 'homework'?
You finish your meal in a restaurant and give the waiter your card to settle the bill.
At the supermarket the cashier says: 'That is 23 euros.' You take out your wallet.
You buy a ticket at the machine and put in coins. Which verb means 'to pay'?
Every Saturday you play on a green field with ten friends. Two teams try to kick a ball into a net.
Your favourite sport has twenty-two players on the field and a referee with a whistle. People shout when a goal is scored.
A boy asks his father to buy him a ball and shoes for the most popular sport in Europe. Which noun means 'soccer, football'?
You look at two shops. The same jeans cost 80 euros in one and only 30 euros in the other. You say the second one is not expensive.
A travel website offers a flight for only 40 euros. Your friend says it is a good price.
You are looking for a hotel and want one that does not cost a lot of money. Which adjective means 'cheap, reasonable'?

en: down, below, at the bottom, downstairs
situations: You live on the ground floor. Your friend lives on the fifth floor and calls you: 'Come up!' You say you are at the bottom of the building.
You look into a deep well and see a coin at the bottom. Where is the coin?
Your jacket is in the cellar. Your sister asks where it is, and you point to the floor and say: 'Downstairs.' Which adverb means 'down below'?
You read a book and turn to the last page. The story stops there.
The film is over and the screen goes black. Your friend says: 'That was the last part, the finish of the story.'
Your holiday is almost over. It is the last day, and tomorrow you go back to work. Which noun means 'end'?
You drive from Munich to Berlin on a wide road with several lanes where there is no speed limit in many places.
The traffic radio says there is a long traffic jam on the big road between two cities near Frankfurt.
Your friend says: 'Take the road with three lanes in each direction, then you arrive faster.' Which noun means 'motorway'?

en: to have to, to need to, to must
situations: The doctor says: 'You are sick. It is not a choice, you have no other way than to stay in bed.' Which verb says that something is necessary?
You tell your friend you cannot go to the cinema because you need to do your homework first.
At the airport the sign says everyone is obliged to show a passport. Which verb means 'to have to'?
You look at the crowd in the station and see thousands of individual beings, each one a member of our species.
A teacher says: 'Every woman, every man and every child is one of these, and all of them have rights.'
A small boy asks his mother if a dog is an animal. She says yes, and then explains that you and he are a different kind of creature: a human being. Which noun means 'human being'?
The doorbell rings and you do not know who stands outside. You ask through the door: '... is there?'
You hear a loud noise in the kitchen. You call out to find the person responsible. Which question word means 'who'?
The phone rings and you pick up. You want to know the name of the person who is calling. Which word do you use to ask 'Who is this?'
In the morning you cannot wake up. You make a hot, dark drink from roasted beans and drink it from a cup.
At a cafe the waiter asks what you want to drink, and you ask for a hot drink with milk and a piece of cake.
Your colleague says: 'I need something with caffeine to stay awake.' Which noun is the answer, the hot drink made from beans?
You eat a very dark chocolate with 90 percent cocoa. It is not sweet at all and has a strong, sharp taste.
You drink tea without sugar and the taste on your tongue is unpleasant, almost like medicine, not sweet.
The opposite of sweet: your friend tastes a lemon peel and makes a face. Which adjective means 'bitter'?
Your teacher asks: 'What is the capital of France?' You say: 'Paris.' What is your reply to the question?
You sent an email to your landlord three days ago and still have not received a reply.
In a quiz you do not know what to say after the host reads the question. Which noun means 'answer'?
It is hot in the room. You go to the window and push it so that fresh air can come in.
The shop has not started yet, but at nine the staff turn the key and let the customers in.
You get a parcel and cut the tape to see what is inside. Which verb means 'to open'?
You live on the eighth floor and your shopping bags are very heavy. You press a button and a small room takes you up.
In the hotel you carry your suitcase into a small cabin with doors and press number 5.
A sign in the building says: 'In case of fire do not use the machine that moves up and down inside the shaft.' Which noun means 'elevator'?
You are late and want to tell your friend. You take the small device from your pocket and send a message.
In the cinema a voice says: 'Please switch off your small device that rings and makes calls.'
You lose your way in a new city and look at the map on the small screen you carry everywhere. Which noun means 'mobile phone'?
Today is Monday. You tell your friend you will meet him on Tuesday.
You say goodbye to your colleague and say: 'See you on the day after today.'
You are tired and say: 'I will do the shopping on the next day, not today.' Which word means 'tomorrow'?
On Sunday you take a train to see your grandmother and stay with her for the afternoon.
You are in Berlin and go to see the museum and the old castle as a tourist.
You go to a language class two evenings a week at the adult school. Which verb means 'to visit' or 'to attend'?
The week has seven days. Wednesday is over and tomorrow is Friday. What day is today?
Your language course meets on Monday and on the day after Wednesday.
Which noun means 'Thursday'?
You want to join a German course and must fill in a form with your name and address before it starts.
You move to a new city and must tell the city office that you live at the new address.
You open a website, type your name and password and click the button to go into your account. Which noun can mean 'registration' or 'login'?
It is Sunday evening. You walk to the supermarket, but the doors are shut and the lights are off.
The sign on the museum door says: 'Not open today, because of holiday.'
At the post office the window is down and the sign says the counter is not in service. Which adjective means 'closed'?
On Saturday night your friends meet at Anna's flat with music, drinks and dancing to celebrate her birthday.
Your neighbours make a lot of noise until 2 a.m. because they invited many guests to celebrate.
Your colleague says: 'On Friday we celebrate the end of the project with food and music in the office.' Which noun means 'party'?

en: to participate, to join in, to take part
situations: Your friends play volleyball at the beach. They ask if you want to be part of the game too, and you say yes.
A teacher asks the whole class to join in a game, and nobody should sit and just watch.
There is a cleaning day in your street, and your neighbour asks if you want to help with the others. Which verb means 'to take part'?
In the exam the teacher says: 'You may write with ink or with the grey writing tool made of wood and graphite.'
You draw a picture and want to be able to rub out the lines with an eraser, so you take the wooden writing tool.
A child puts a long, thin wooden writing tool with a sharp point into his school bag. Which noun means 'pencil'?
The sun comes up in the morning. In which direction do you look to see it rise?
On a map the compass shows north on top. The side on the right, the direction opposite to west, is this one.
You live in Berlin and your friend lives far away in the direction where the sun rises. Which noun means 'east'?
You grew up in a small village, but now you live in a big place with many streets, shops, trains and thousands of people.
Munich, Hamburg and Cologne are examples of what? They are places with a lot of houses and a centre with a town hall.
A friend says: 'I want to move from the countryside to a place with more jobs, cafes and cinemas.' Which noun means 'city, town'?
Your friend has no pen. You take yours and put it into her hand.
At the dinner table your father asks you to pass him the salt. What do you do with the salt?
The teacher hands each pupil a sheet of paper. Which verb means 'to give'?
Your teacher asks how you did in the exam. You answer that it went fine, not badly at all.
A friend plays the piano and you listen. You say that she plays in a very nice way, not badly.
Someone asks: 'How are you?' and you say you are fine. Which adverb means 'well'?
Your friend wants to hand you a gift. He says: 'This is for ...' and points at you. Which word means 'to me' or 'me'?
At the bookshop you ask the clerk to show a book to you. 'Can you show it to ...?' Which small word do you use?
A friend is cooking. You say: 'Could you pass the salt to ..., please?' Which pronoun means 'me' after 'to'?
You buy a long yellow fruit with a thick peel that grows in warm countries. Monkeys love it.
For a quick snack before sport you peel a soft, sweet fruit, which is yellow and curved.
At the market you buy apples, oranges and a bunch of curved fruits. Which word means 'banana'?
At the university there are students from Brazil, India, Nigeria and Japan. The group is not only from one country.
The airport has flights to many countries. The sign shows the terminal for flights that cross borders.
A company has offices in twenty countries around the world. Which adjective describes such a company: not local, but between nations?
You and your family live in a building with a roof, a front door and a garden. It is not a flat.
An architect draws a plan for a new building with four rooms and a kitchen for a young family.
At the end of a long day you say: 'I want to go to the place where I live and feel safe.' Which noun means 'house, home'?

en: to earn, to deserve, to merit
situations: At the end of the month the company puts money into your bank account for your work.
You ask your uncle how much money he gets every month from his job as an engineer.
A child cleans the whole kitchen and her mother says: 'You really deserve a reward.' Which verb can mean 'to earn' or 'to deserve'?

en: management, command, leadership, guided tour, lead
situations: In the old town a woman walks with your group and tells you the history of each building. What is this tour called?
A manager says that the company needs strong leaders. Which noun means the act of leading people at work?
At a museum a sign says: 'Tours at 10 and 14 o'clock with a guide.' Which noun means 'guided tour' or 'leadership'?
You ride to work every morning on two wheels, turning the pedals with your feet.
The shop sells things with two wheels, a chain, a saddle and a bell. You buy one for your son.
The train is too expensive, so you decide to go to the lake on something with pedals and a chain. Which noun means 'bicycle'?
People in the north of the country use a second name for the day after Friday and before Sunday. Which day is that?
Your colleague from Hamburg says: 'We meet on the weekend's first day.' It is the day between Friday and Sunday.
Which word means 'Saturday' in the north of Germany?
In the restaurant you tell the waiter: 'I would like the soup and a glass of water.'
You are at home and want a new book. You go on a website and ask the shop to send it to you.
At the cafe the waiter comes to your table and asks what you want to eat and drink. What do you do now? Which verb means 'to order'?
Every Tuesday and Thursday evening you go to a room with a teacher and other adults to learn German.
At the bank you want to change dollars into euros. The clerk tells you how many euros you get for one dollar today.
At the gym there is a group lesson for yoga that runs for eight weeks. Which noun means 'course'?
You meet a man from Berlin. You ask where he comes from and he says: 'I come from Germany.' Which adjective describes his nationality?
At a restaurant the menu says the sausage and the beer are made the way people in Germany make them.
Your friend learns the language that is spoken in Germany, Austria and part of Switzerland. Which adjective means 'German'?
After work and at weekends you go swimming, meet friends and read books, without anything you must do.
A form asks about your hobbies. You write: football, cinema and cooking, things you do when you are not at work or school.
Your boss asks what you do when you are not working. You answer: 'I use my spare hours for sport.' Which noun means 'free time'?
Your friend asks: 'Do you want to come with us to the cinema?' You answer that you will come and that it makes you happy.
You say: 'I ... play tennis', meaning that you like to play it.
A colleague asks you to help with something and you say you will do it with pleasure. Which adverb means 'gladly'?
At the restaurant the waiter brings a list of dishes and drinks, and you choose your meal.
You are lost in a new city, so you open a paper sheet that shows all the streets and parks.
You pay at the shop with a small plastic rectangle from your bank. Which noun can mean 'card', 'map', 'menu' or 'ticket'?

en: to hike, to migrate, to wander
situations: On Sunday you put on strong shoes, take a backpack and walk for six hours in the mountains.
Your friends love nature, so they spend their holidays walking along paths through forests and over hills.
Birds fly south in the autumn. What do many animals do when they move from one region to another? Which verb means 'to hike' or 'to migrate'?
A man works for the city office and has a safe job for life, working for the state. He sits behind a desk and stamps papers.
At the town hall the man behind the counter says: 'I am a state employee and I cannot do that for you.'
Your uncle works in a government job with a secure position. Which noun means 'civil servant' (male)?
At eight o'clock the teacher comes into the room, closes the door and starts teaching the whole class.
Your son says: 'Today there was no school because the teacher was sick.' What did not happen?
A student says he missed the teaching on Monday because he was sick. Which noun means 'lessons, class'?
You go into the toilet on the train and the door is locked with a red sign. Somebody is inside.
You call your friend, but you hear a beeping sound because he is already talking to someone else.
In a restaurant a man points to the free chair and you ask: 'Is this seat free?' He says: 'No, someone is sitting there.' Which adjective means 'occupied'?
A guest comes into your flat. You say: 'Would you like some tea?' and hold out a cup.
A shop wants you to buy more. It says on the poster: 'We give you a free bag if you buy two shirts.'
Your colleague says to the new person: 'If you need help, just ask. I can help you with it.' Which verb means 'to offer'?
You walk to the end of the street and turn left where two walls or streets meet.
Your sofa stands in the place of the room where two walls meet, next to the lamp.
A friend asks where the bakery is. You say: 'It is right where this street meets the next one.' Which noun means 'corner'?
You meet your new teacher for the first time and want to be polite. You do not say the word for 'you' that you use with friends. Which word means 'you' in the polite form?
A clerk at the bank speaks to an older customer and asks: '... are next.' Which word means formal 'you'?
You talk to a stranger on the street and ask for the way. Which pronoun do you use for polite 'you'?
A, B, C and D are all examples of what? The alphabet has 26 of them.
On the phone you spell your name one by one for the clerk: 'M as in Maria, I as in Ida...'
A child learns to write the first sign of the alphabet. Which noun means 'letter (of the alphabet)'?
For breakfast you boil a white oval food with a shell for five minutes and eat it with salt.
A hen lays them every morning. You use some of them to make a cake.
At the supermarket you buy a box of six, which come from chickens. Which word means 'egg'?
You are waiting for your friend at the bus stop. He calls and says he will be there in a few minutes, not later.
A teacher says: 'The holidays are nearly here. Only two more days!' Which word means 'soon'?
The doctor says: 'You will be healthy again in the near future.' Which adverb means 'soon'?
It is hot, so you jump into the lake and move your arms and legs to stay on the water.
At the swimming pool the lifeguard asks: 'Can you move in the water without touching the ground?'
A piece of wood falls into the river and stays on top of the water. Which verb means 'to swim, to float'?
In maths class the teacher asks for the correct result to the problem on the board.
Your computer does not start. A friend finds a way to fix the problem and says: 'Here is what we do.'
In a quiz book the answers to all the questions are on the last page. Which noun means 'solution'?
You put a round shiny disc into the player to listen to your favourite band's album.
In an old car there is no streaming, only a slot for a flat silver disc with music.
At a music shop you buy a plastic case with a round disc inside. Which word is the short form for 'compact disc'?
Your grandmother is 80 years old, but her granddaughter is only 6. How would you describe the little girl in terms of age?
The new colleague is only 22 and has just finished school. Your boss says that he is not old.
A teacher says: 'I want to work with people who have not lived many years.' Which adjective means 'young'?
At the restaurant you stand up and ask the waiter where you can wash your hands and go to the room with a sink.
In the train station you pay 50 cents to use a public room with a sink and a bowl.
A child says: 'Mum, I need to go to the place where you go when you must go.' Which noun means 'restroom'?

en: to begin, to start, to commence
situations: The film is at 8 o'clock. You sit in the cinema and the lights go out. The film is starting now.
The teacher says: 'Please open your books. We will now take the first page.' What does the lesson do?
In the morning your meeting does not start until 9. You ask: 'When does it commence?' Which verb means 'to begin'?
You live in Hamburg, and in winter you travel to a warm region where the sun is high at noon, towards Italy.
On a compass the needle points to the north and the opposite direction is this one.
Bavaria lies in the part of Germany that is at the bottom of the map. Which noun means 'south'?
On Sunday you visit an old woman who is your mother's mother. She bakes cakes and tells stories.
A child says: 'My mum's mum lives in the countryside, and I go there in summer.'
At a family party the oldest woman in the room is the mother of your father. Which noun means 'grandmother'?

en: to meet, to make, to hit, to strike
situations: After work you go to a cafe where your friend is waiting. You see each other and talk for an hour.
The ball flies towards the goal and hits the post. Which verb describes when something hits a target?
You arrange with a colleague that you will see each other at the station at 6. Which verb means 'to meet'?
A shop sign says: 'Everything is 20 of these cheaper!' The sign shows a symbol: %.
At the bank you get 2 of every 100 euros as interest each year. How is this part of one hundred called?
In the news you hear that 5 out of every 100 people are out of work. Which noun means 'per cent'?
You ask: 'How many euros do you have?' and your friend says: 'Just two, not more.' Which word means 'only'?
A waiter asks if you want a dessert. You say that you want a coffee and nothing else.
You tell your boss: 'I did not do anything special. I did that one small thing.' Which adverb means 'only, just'?
You have something in your eye, so you close it and rub it. You have two of them, and you use them to see.
The optician says: 'Please cover your left one and read the letters on the wall with your right.'
A child draws a face with a nose, a mouth, ears and two round things to see with. Which noun means 'eye'?
Your friend wins the lottery and jumps around with a big smile. How does she feel?
A little boy gets a puppy for his birthday and laughs all day. How would you describe him?
You say: 'I feel great today. Everything is going well.' Which adjective means 'happy'?
You wait under a roof next to a sign with a number. In five minutes the bus comes.
A tram stops in the street and people get on and off at the sign with the line number. Where do they wait?
A friend says: 'Get off at the next place where the bus stops, and then walk two minutes.' Which noun means 'stop' (for buses and trams)?
Every day from 9 to 5 you sit in an office, write emails and have meetings. What do you do?
Your father gets up at six to go to the factory, where he does his job as a mechanic.
A friend asks what you do during the week. You say that you have a job in a hospital. Which verb means 'to work'?
A woman walks into the shop to buy a coat. The salesman says: 'Welcome. How can I help you?' What is she in the shop?
At the hairdresser's the boss says: 'The woman who is waiting there buys our services.' Which word describes her?
In a bank a female clerk speaks to a woman who has an account there. Which noun means 'customer' (female)?
You talk to your two friends at the same time and ask: 'Are ... coming to the party?' Which word means 'you' for more than one friend?
In the class the teacher looks at all the children and says: 'Please sit down, ...' Which pronoun is used when talking to several people informally?
You point to your sister's bag: 'This is ... bag.' You mean it belongs to her. Which word means 'her' before a noun?
A boy of 15 is no longer a child, but not yet an adult. He plays football with his friends after school.
A youth club is open to people between 13 and 18. Today a young boy from the neighbourhood joins for the first time.
The police officer says: 'A teenage boy broke the window.' Which noun means 'adolescent' (male)?
The sixth month of the year starts after May and ends before July. School holidays are nearly here.
Your birthday is in the month when summer begins, in the northern part of the world, around 21st.
You write the date on a form: 15 ... 2025. Which noun means 'June'?

en: to get off, to get out, to disembark
situations: The train arrives in Munich. You stand up, take your bag and step out onto the platform.
The bus driver says: 'This is the last stop. Everyone must leave the bus now.'
