You take a taxi to the station, and when you arrive you open the door and step out. Which verb means 'to get off, to get out'?
Eleven players in the same shirts walk onto the field together. What is this group called, as a sports group?
On a ship, the captain gives orders to all the people who work on board and sail it together.
At school your class plays volleyball against another class. You are all part of one group that wins or loses together. Which noun means 'team'?
Your friend calls while you are cooking. You say: 'I cannot talk now. I will call you after dinner, not now.'
The bus does not come at 8:00. It comes at 8:30, after the time you planned. Which adjective compares the time?
The boss says: 'Please come to my office in the afternoon, not this morning.' Which word means 'later'?
You put a white sheet in the printer and write a letter on it. Which material is the sheet made of?
At school you tear a page out of your notebook and make a small boat out of it.
At the recycling station there are separate bins for glass, plastic and old newspapers and boxes made from trees. Which noun means 'paper'?
You come to the pharmacy at 9 p.m. The door will not move and the lights are off, so it is shut. Which word describes it?
You say that the soup is more salty than you like: 'This is ... much salt.' Which word means 'too'?
On a door a small sign says that the shop is not open right now. Which word, shorter than a sentence, means 'closed'?
You read job advertisements and see that a company is looking for a new accountant. It has a free position.
A policeman asks you to show on the map exactly the spot where the accident happened.
You wait in line and somebody asks you: 'Can you hold my place?' Which noun means 'place' or 'position'?
You look at the price tag of a coat: 120 euros. You ask the seller: 'How much does it ... ?'
At the market the seller gives you a small piece of cheese so you can find out how it tastes before you buy it.
The waiter says: 'Would you like to try our new soup?' You put a spoonful in your mouth. Which verb can mean 'to cost' or 'to taste'?
Every morning your father reads a big paper with news, sports and weather while he drinks tea.
At the kiosk you buy something that is printed every day, with headlines on the front page.
A man on the train opens the pages wide and reads about politics and football. Which noun means 'newspaper'?
A tall person with a beard walks into the shop. He is an adult, but not a woman or a boy.
At a wedding the bride stands next to her partner. Her friend says: 'This is the person she married.'
You say: 'My sister's partner is a nice person.' You mean the person who is married to her. Which noun means 'man' or 'husband'?
Your child asks if he may stay up until 10 o'clock. You say: 'Yes, I will let you.'
A sign in the park says that dogs are not allowed unless they are on a lead. What does the sign decide?
The teacher says: 'You may use a dictionary in the exam.' She gives you permission. Which verb means 'to allow'?
At the market the seller says: 'No cards, please. Only notes and coins.' How do you pay?
You find a discount: 'Pay with real money, not with a card, and get 5 percent off.' Which adjective describes this kind of payment?
You do not have a bank card, so you hand over notes and coins at the till. Which adjective means 'cash'?
A small male child plays with a ball in the park. He is not yet a teenager.
A mother says to her friend: 'I have a girl and a young male child. Both are at primary school.'
At the zoo a teacher counts: 'There are twelve girls and eight male children in our class.' Which noun means 'boy'?
You rent a flat. Every month you pay money to the woman who owns the building and the flat.
The heating in your flat is broken. You call the woman who owns the house and ask her to send someone.
A neighbour says: 'The lady who has let me this flat is very nice.' Which noun means 'landlady'?
A newspaper writes that a big company earns a very large number: 1,000 million euros in one year.
A teacher says that the world has over eight of these people, meaning eight thousand millions.
In maths you write 1,000,000,000. Which noun means 'billion', a thousand millions?

en: to end, to terminate, to cease
situations: The film is over, the screen goes black, and the music stops. The story is finished.
Your contract with the phone company runs until 31 December, and then it stops.
The teacher looks at the clock and says: 'The lesson finishes in a minute.' Which verb means 'to end'?

en: his, its, their, one's, his or her
situations: You point to the coat of your brother on the chair: 'This is ... coat.' Which word means 'his'?
A dog has a bone and holds it between its teeth. 'The dog eats ... bone.' Which word means 'its'?
A colleague has forgotten his umbrella. You say to him: 'Is this ... umbrella over there?' Which possessive word means 'his'?
You go swimming on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays. Your friend asks how many times you go, and you answer: 'Many times a week.'
Your neighbour visits his mother every day or almost every day. Which adverb describes how frequently he visits?
A friend asks if you cook at home. You say: 'Yes, I cook most evenings, not rarely.' Which adverb means 'often'?
Monday, Tuesday and Friday are examples. Which word do we use for any of the days from Monday to Sunday, such as when a form asks which one you choose?
You ask your colleague: 'On which one of the seven days does the course meet?' Which noun is the general word for such a day?
A teacher writes the names of the days on the board. Which noun means 'day of the week'?
A man and a woman stand in front of the guests and say 'yes' to each other. The bride wears a white dress.
Your cousin sends invitation cards with two rings on them for a big party after the ceremony in the church.
Your friend is getting married next month and you buy a present. Which noun means 'wedding'?
You mix red, yellow and black paint and get the colour of chocolate or tree trunks.
Your friend has dark hair and eyes the colour of coffee. Which colour is it?
Autumn leaves, wooden tables and bears often have this colour. Which adjective means 'brown'?
You finish reading a book and the last chapter ends the story. The author wrote a satisfying one.
At work your boss says: 'It is five o'clock, time to stop for today.' The day is over.
In the lesson the teacher says: 'To conclude, let me summarise.' Which noun means 'end, conclusion'?
You take a pen and write your address on the form.
The hotel says: 'Guests can make use of the swimming pool until 10 p.m.'
You don't have a car, so you take the bus to work every day. Which verb means 'to use'?
A woman says about the man she married: 'The man I live with and love has a job at the bank.'
On a form for women there is a line for the name of the person you are married to.
Your sister's partner became her legal husband last year. Which noun means 'husband'?
Today you are 30. Your friends sing, give you presents and bring a cake with candles.
On a form you must write the day, month and year when you were born.
A colleague asks: 'When is your special day every year, when you become one year older?' Which noun means 'birthday'?

en: to sign up, to log in, to register, to enrol, to subscribe
situations: You want to start swimming lessons. You go to the sports centre and put your name on the list.
You open an online shop, type your name and password and go into your account.
You move to a new town and tell the city office that your address has changed. Which verb means 'to register, to sign up'?
It is dark in the room. You press the switch and the lamp makes everything bright.
In the morning sunshine comes in through the window, so you do not need the lamp.
A friend says: 'Please turn off the lamp before you go.' Which noun means 'light'?
In class you raise your hand because there is something you do not understand and you want to ask.
The teacher writes a sentence that ends with a question mark. What is it?
At the end of the talk the speaker says: 'Does anyone have a ... ?' Which noun means 'question'?
You come to the shop at 10 a.m. The door is not locked and a sign says you can enter. Which word describes the shop?
The window is wide open and the fresh air comes in. Which word means 'open'?
The teacher says: 'Stand ...!' and you get to your feet. Which short word means 'up'?
A basketball player is 2 meters tall. Compared to others, how is he?
You live in a flat with a lot of space, with a huge living room. Which adjective describes the size of the room?
A small child looks at an elephant and says: 'It is not small, it is ...!' Which adjective means 'big'?
Every morning your father goes to the office to do what he does to earn money. What is it?
A teacher says: 'Please hand in your written paper on Friday.' She means the test or essay.
In the evening you tell your friend: 'I am tired because there was a lot to do at the office today.' Which noun means 'work'?
You do not know where the station is, so you speak to a person on the street and want to know the way.
In class a student puts up his hand and wants to know the meaning of a word.
You want to know the time and look at your neighbour on the bus with a question. Which verb means 'to ask'?
A man sits behind the wheel of a bus and takes people from stop to stop.
In a taxi you tell the man at the wheel the address where you want to go.
A sign on the truck says: 'The man who drives this lorry has no money in the cab.' Which noun means 'driver' (male)?
You put your wallet and keys into a thing with a handle that you carry on your shoulder.
You put your hands into the small space in your trousers because it is cold.
A woman takes her phone and her makeup out of the thing she carries with her. Which noun means 'bag' or 'pocket'?
After December the new year begins. What is the first month, when it is cold and many people make resolutions?
You celebrate New Year's Day on the first day of this month.
On a calendar you look at the first page of twelve. Which noun means 'January'?
In summer you take a plane to Spain, then a bus to Portugal, and you see many places.
Your uncle is a pilot and he is away from home most weeks, going to other countries and cities.
A friend asks what you like to do on holiday. You say: 'I like to go to new places far away.' Which verb means 'to travel'?
You see your two friends' car outside the cafe and ask: 'Is this ... car?' Which word means 'your' for two or more friends?
You talk to a group of classmates: 'Where is ... teacher today?' Which possessive means 'your' (several people, informal)?
Two neighbours have a dog. You ask them: 'Does ... dog bark at night?' Which word means 'your' for them?
At the market you ask the seller for 1,000 grams of apples. What is the unit of weight?
You step on the scale and it shows 70. The scale measures in this unit.
A recipe asks for two of them of potatoes. Which noun means 'kilogram'?
You walk on a road with four lanes. It is not narrow at all. How would you describe the road?
The river is so far from one side to the other that you cannot throw a stone over it.
The opposite of narrow: your sofa does not fit through the door because it is too ... Which adjective means 'wide'?
The sky is grey and water falls from the clouds. You take your umbrella.
Your friend says: 'We cannot have a picnic today, because drops of water are falling.'
The weather forecast says: 'Tomorrow, wet weather in the whole country.' Which noun means 'rain'?
Everyone else went to the party, but you stay at home without anybody around you.
A child says: 'I can do it by myself, I don't need help!' Which word means 'by oneself, alone'?
Your friend lives in a flat and has no flatmates or family there. Which adverb means 'alone'?
Your friend tells a very funny joke and you cannot stop making happy sounds and smiling widely.
A comedy on TV is so good that the whole audience is making loud happy noises.
A baby sees a funny face and makes a happy sound. What does the baby do? Which verb means 'to laugh'?
On a camping trip you sit around hot orange flames, make warm food and tell stories.
The alarm goes off in the building and the fire brigade arrives because something is burning.
A child plays with matches. His mother says: 'Careful! That can start something that burns.' Which noun means 'fire'?
A clock has hours, and each hour has sixty of these. Which unit is shorter than an hour and longer than a second?
Your friend says: 'Wait, I need just sixty seconds to finish.' What does she mean?
The bus comes in five of them. Which noun means 'minute'?
You arrive at the hotel and go to the desk in the entrance hall to get your room key.
At a big company a visitor reports at the desk near the door and the staff there call your contact.
You ask at the hotel where you can ask about breakfast times. The staff point to the front desk. Which noun means 'reception'?

en: to stand up, to get up
situations: The alarm clock rings at 6:30. You throw back the blanket and get out of bed.
In the classroom the teacher enters, and the students all rise from their chairs.
On the bus an old woman is looking for a seat. You leave yours for her. Which verb means 'to get up, to stand up'?
The queue at the post office reaches from the counter to the door. How would you describe the queue?
Your friend has hair that reaches down to her waist.
The film lasts more than three hours. You say it is not short. Which adjective means 'long'?
In the restaurant the waiter hands you a card with all the dishes and their prices.
You want to know if there are vegetarian dishes, so you ask the waiter for the list of food.
A guest at the table says: 'Could I have the list of dishes, please?' Which noun means 'menu'?
You are a student and work in a cafe on weekends to earn some money.
A friend asks what you do. You say: 'I have a part-time position at a supermarket.'
Which noun, borrowed from English, means 'job'?
You do not work for two weeks and you go to the beach with your family.
You ask your boss for time off in August because you want to travel to Italy.
A colleague is away from the office. The secretary says: 'He is on his holiday until Monday.' Which noun means 'holiday, vacation'?
After your trip your friends ask you about it, and you speak for an hour about what you saw.
A grandfather sits with his grandchildren and speaks about his childhood in a small village.
At bedtime a mother says a story to her child. Which verb means 'to tell' (a story)?
It is cold in the evening, so you put on a warm piece of clothing with sleeves and a zip over your shirt.
In the shop you try on a short piece of clothing with pockets that you wear over your sweater.
The weather has changed and your friend says: 'Take something to wear over your shirt.' Which noun means 'jacket'?
You point at a shop on the other side of the street and say: 'I bought my shoes at that place, not here.'
A friend asks where the bank is. You point to the corner and say: 'It is at that spot.'
You are in a restaurant and your friend sits far away at another table. You point and say: 'She is ...'. Which adverb means 'there'?
After summer the school year begins in this month, which comes after August.
The leaves start to turn yellow and the ninth month of the year begins.
On a calendar the ninth page shows this month. Which noun means 'September'?
A friend from India says: 'I am not from this country, and my passport is from another one.' What type of person is this?
In the supermarket there is a section with food from other countries, like Italy and Japan.
A form asks whether your qualification comes from your own country or from another country. Which adjective means 'foreign'?

en: to leave, to depart, to drive off
situations: You stand on the platform. At 8:15 the train starts moving out of the station.
The bus driver starts the engine and the bus leaves the stop with all passengers on board.
The guide says: 'We start at 9 sharp, please be on time.' Which verb means 'to depart'?
In the kitchen you put a pot of soup on the hot plate and turn the knob.
You bake a pizza in the oven under the part with the hot rings in your kitchen.
The kitchen has a fridge, a sink and the appliance with four hot plates where you cook. Which noun means 'cooker, stove'?

en: much, a lot of, lots of, many
situations: In a very busy shop you say: 'There are a great number of people here.' Which word means 'many, a lot of'?
A friend asks if you have any money. You answer that you have a large amount, not just a little.
You say: 'I work a large amount these days, and I'm tired.' Which word means 'much, a lot'?
The school day has several periods, each lasting 45 minutes. Which noun do the students use for one period?
You wait for the doctor. The nurse says: 'It will be 60 minutes.' What unit of time does she use?
The film is two of them long. Which noun means 'hour' or 'lesson'?
You have a pain in the part of the body on top of your neck, and you take a pill.
You put a hat on the part of the body where your hair and your eyes are.
A teacher says: 'Please use what is inside your skull and think.' Which noun means 'head' or 'mind'?
Your colleague has a baby. You shake her hand and say: 'All the best, I am happy for you!'
Your friend passes his driving test. You send a message saying well done.
At a birthday party you say: 'Happy birthday!' to the person with the cake. Which verb means 'to congratulate'?
A person at the shop wears a dress and has long hair. She is an adult, but not a man.
A man introduces the person he is married to: 'This is my partner, I have been married to her for ten years.'
On a letter you write the title before a name: 'Dear ... Schmidt.' Which noun means 'woman', 'wife' or 'Mrs.'?
The police officer asks the witness to tell what she saw. What she says is written down.
In court a man tells what he knows about the crime. Which noun means what he says as a witness?
A teacher says: 'Read the sentence. Is its claim true or false?' Which noun means 'statement'?
Your friend asks: 'Can we meet tomorrow?' You check your calendar. You think it can happen, there is no problem.
Your boss asks for a report. You say it can be done by Friday if you start now.
The opposite of impossible: a plan that can work. Which adjective means 'possible'?
You ask your colleague if he has eaten lunch, and he says yes, he did that earlier than you thought.
The film is only starting at 8, but your friend is at the cinema at 7. You say: 'You are early.'
A teacher asks: 'Have you finished the task?' You say: 'Yes, I did it a while ago.' Which adverb means 'already'?
Monday to Sunday: that is seven days. What is this period of time called?
Your holiday lasts seven days. You say: 'We are going away for one of them.'
A language course meets twice every one of these, on Tuesday and Thursday. Which noun means 'week'?

en: to stop, to hold, to keep, to last
situations: A bus driver brings the bus to a stop at the red light.
You stand with a cup of tea and do not put it down. You keep it in your hand.
The teacher says: 'Hold the line and don't let go of the rope.' Which verb can mean 'to stop' or 'to hold'?
You write a letter on your laptop and then send it to a machine that puts it on a sheet of paper.
At the office the machine is empty. You need to put in more ink and paper so people can print their documents.
Your homework is on the computer, but your teacher wants it on paper. You use a device. Which noun means 'printer'?
A woman stays at home all day. She cooks, cleans and looks after the children and has no job outside.
A form asks for your job. A woman writes that she looks after her house and family.
My neighbour does not work in an office. She runs the household. Which noun means 'housewife'?
At the start of a letter you write 'Dear Sir' or 'Dear Madam'. What is this part of the letter called?
A form asks whether you want to be called Mr, Mrs or Ms. What does the line ask for?
Before the name in an email you write a polite greeting. Which noun means 'salutation'?
You are sitting at the window with your eyes closed. A bird is singing and you notice the sound.
You put on headphones and enjoy a song on purpose.
The teacher says: 'Pay attention to the music and the sounds on the recording.' Which verb means 'to hear' or 'to listen'?
The device on the table rings. You pick up the receiver and say hello.
You want to call your grandmother, who has an old device with a cable on the wall.
At the hotel the staff say: 'You can call the reception from the device in your room.' Which noun means 'telephone'?
You taste the cake your friend baked and it is delicious. How would you describe it?
The teacher reads your test and says the work is better than most, nothing wrong. Which adjective describes it?
A friend asks about the movie. You say it is very enjoyable, not bad. Which adjective means 'good'?
A form asks in which town you were born, for example Dhaka or Berlin.
At the passport office the clerk asks: 'Where did you come into the world?' She wants the name of a city.
On an ID card there is a line with the name of the town where you were born. Which noun means 'place of birth'?
You and your family own a house. You tell a visitor: 'This is ... house.' Which word means 'our'?
You and your friends have a football team. You say: 'We love ... team.' Which possessive means 'our'?
At school you and your classmate say: 'This is ... teacher.' Which word means 'our'?

en: to take, to take along, to give a lift
situations: You go on a trip and put your umbrella into your bag so that you have it with you.
Your colleague goes the same way home by car and says: 'Hop in, I can drive you.'
You are going to the party. Your friend says: 'Don't forget to bring a gift along.' Which verb means 'to take along'?
You live in a village outside the city. Every morning you take a fast electric train that goes between the suburbs and the centre.
At the station the sign shows lines S1 and S2. These trains run more often than long-distance trains.
In Munich you take the city train underground and above ground. Which noun means 'suburban train'?
Every day, without exception, you drink a glass of milk before bed. How often do you do it?
A friend says: 'You are late again!' You answer: 'No, I am on time every single time.' Which adverb fits?
Your mother says: 'You can count on me at all times.' Which adverb means 'always'?
At the airport you must walk through a gate where officers check whether you carry goods you must declare.
You buy a watch in another country and have to pay extra money when you bring it home.
In the car shop a man says: 'This screen is 15 of these wide.' Which noun can mean 'customs' or a measure of length (inch)?
After February, spring begins in this month. It is the third month of the year.
The days get longer and the clocks change to summer time at the end of this month.
On a calendar the third page shows this month. Which noun means 'March'?

en: to belong to, to be part of
situations: You see a jacket on the chair and ask: 'Whose is this?' Your friend says: 'It is mine, I own it.'
A boy says: 'I am a member of the football team.' He is part of it.
You find a lost bag and ask the people nearby if it is theirs. Which verb means 'to belong to'?
A form asks: 'Married, divorced or ...?' A man who has never married ticks this box.
At a party your friend says: 'I have no husband or wife and no partner.' Which adjective describes his marital status?
On the registration form, your marital status is the opposite of married. Which adjective means 'single'?
On the motorway a very big vehicle with a trailer carries boxes and goods from one city to another.
A man drives a large vehicle that delivers furniture to the shop, and he parks it behind the building.
The road sign shows a symbol of a big vehicle for transporting goods. Which noun means 'truck, lorry'?
On a form there are two lines. The first asks for your given name, the second for the name that you share with your parents and brothers.
At the doctor's office the nurse calls: 'Mr Müller, please come in.' She calls your name that you share with your family.
You and your sister have the same name that comes from your father. Which noun means 'surname'?
The days are short and grey, and the eleventh month of the year begins after October.
The trees have lost their leaves and the cold weather has started. Christmas is not far.
On a calendar the eleventh page shows this month. Which noun means 'November'?
You meet a new person and ask for his name: 'What is your name?'
You introduce yourself: 'My name is Anna.' What does your name do?
A student asks the teacher what a word means in English. Which verb means 'to be called' or 'to mean'?
A child says: 'Mum's father tells us stories and plays chess with me.' How does the child call him in a friendly, short way?
At a family party the youngest children run to the old man with white hair and call him by a short, loving name.
On Sunday you visit your father's father. Which noun means 'grandpa'?
A friend says: 'There is a great cafe on the corner.' You answer: 'Let's go to that place now.' Which word means 'to there'?
You see a beautiful beach on a photo. You say: 'I want to travel to that place next summer.'
You point at the museum across the river and say: 'Let's walk in that direction.' Which adverb means 'to there'?
Five tourists follow the guide through the old town. Together they are a small number of people.
A teacher divides the class: 'Four students work together on one task.' What are these four students?
At the language school there are beginners and advanced learners, each of them sitting in a separate room. Which noun means 'group'?
Your host welcomes you at the door with a big smile and a hug, and says: 'Come in, we are happy to see you!'
At the end of a letter you write: 'With kind regards.' The adjective describes the greeting as friendly and from the heart.
A hotel manager gives you a friendly reception. Which adjective means 'warm, cordial'?
A child asks: 'Can I play outside?' Her mother says yes. What does the child ask for?
A sign in the museum says that photos are permitted, but not with flash.
You ask the teacher: 'Am I permitted to go to the toilet?' Which verb means 'to be allowed to'?
At the family party you meet your uncle, your cousin and your aunt. They are all members of your extended family. How do you call a male family member who is not your parent?
A man at the wedding says: 'He is my father's brother's son. He is part of my family.' Which word describes him?
A form asks for the name of a male member of your family to call in an emergency. Which noun means 'relative' (male)?
You open a book and read the first page. The story is just beginning.
The teacher says: 'Let's go back to the first lines of the text.'
The film started at eight. You arrived late and missed the first minutes. Which noun means 'beginning'?
You sit at a desk with a computer and a phone in the office where you work every day.
A company says it will open fifty new positions for workers in the factory.
Your boss says: 'Please keep the table and the area where you work clean.' Which noun means 'workplace'?
At the bank, you speak to an older customer and ask politely: 'Is this ... bag?' Which formal word means 'your'?
In an email to a stranger you write: 'Thank you for ... help.' Which polite word means 'your'?
The doctor asks a patient he does not know: 'What is ... name?' Which formal possessive means 'your'?

en: to run, to go, to walk
situations: You put on sports shoes and move quickly along the river, but not fast enough to sprint.
The bus is late, so you move on your feet for twenty minutes to get to work.
A child moves on two legs faster and faster across the field. Which verb can mean 'to run' or 'to walk'?
On a form there are two lines. One is for the name you share with your family; the other is for the name your parents chose for you alone.
At the doctor's office the nurse calls you with the name your friends use when they talk to you, like Anna or Peter.
On your name tag at the conference, you write only the name that comes first, like Maria. Which noun means 'first name'?
You go to a big place with terminals where planes take off and land, to catch your flight to London.
A taxi driver asks where to take you. You say you need to get to the place with runways and check-in desks.
Your friend is arriving from abroad and you drive to pick him up. Where do you go? Which noun means 'airport'?
Yesterday you had a cold, but today you feel less ill. How do you feel compared to yesterday?
Your friend plays tennis very well. After training with a coach, she plays at an even higher level.
You try two jackets and prefer one over the other. You say it is the superior one. Which adjective means 'better'?
On a hot day you take your towel and go to a public place with water, a diving board and lifeguards.
Every Saturday your children go to a building with a big basin of water, where they have their lessons.
You ask a friend: 'Do you want to swim today?' He says: 'Yes, let's go to the public pool.' Which noun means 'swimming pool'?
You are cold and want a warm coat. You say: 'I cannot go without one.'
A friend asks if you want any help with the move. You say: 'Yes, I really have to have someone to carry the boxes.'
A child tells his mother: 'I must have a new pencil for school.' Which verb means 'to need'?
You and your friend go to the cinema. You are not alone; one goes with the other.
The whole family sits at one table to eat dinner, not separately.
Your colleague asks: 'Shall we go to lunch ...?' Which adverb means 'together'?
At a fancy restaurant the waiter says: 'Good evening, ladies and gentlemen.' He speaks to an elegant, polite woman in a long dress. How do you call such a woman?
A sign on the door of a washroom shows a woman in a dress. A friend says it is for the female guests, in a formal style.
In a board game you move round pieces diagonally on a black and white board, and one piece is called 'queen' in chess. Which noun can mean 'lady' or 'queen' (in cards or chess)?
Your three-year-old son goes to a place every morning where children play, sing and paint before school age.
A mother drops her daughter at a building with a playground and a teacher, and goes to work. The child is too young for school.
A parent asks the neighbour where the children play together and learn before their first school year. Which noun means 'nursery school'?
You are on the bus and all the chairs are taken, but you have found a place and rest your legs.
A bird lands on the branch of a tree and stays on it without moving.
You work at a desk all day. Your back hurts because you rest on a chair for eight hours. Which verb means 'to sit'?
In summer the sky is blue and a big yellow ball gives you light and heat. You put on sun cream.
You close the curtains because the bright star in the sky shines straight into your face.
The earth goes round it once a year. Which noun means 'sun'?
On Saturday evening you and your partner go to a place where waiters bring food to your table and you pay at the end.
You do not feel like cooking tonight, so you phone to reserve a table for four at 8 p.m.
Your friend says: 'Let's eat out. There is a nice Italian place near the station.' Which noun means 'restaurant'?
You draw the curtains in the morning and the room is full of sunshine, not dark at all.
A shop sells paint in colours such as dark blue and pale blue. You choose the colour with more white in it.
A lamp shines so strongly that your eyes hurt. Which adjective means 'light' or 'bright'?
On Sundays you visit a kind old woman who bakes apple cake. She is the mother of your mum.
A little girl runs to the door and shouts that her dad's mother has arrived with a bag of presents. What does she call her in a warm, short way?
At the family party the youngest child sits on the lap of the white-haired woman and calls her by a loving name. Which noun means 'grandma'?
It is dark in the living room. You press the switch and make the lamp work.
Your friend wants to watch the news, so he presses the button on the remote and the screen starts up.
In winter you put a match to the wood so that the fireplace starts burning. Which verb means 'to turn on' or 'to light'?
At work you have a problem. You knock on the door of the person who is in charge of the whole department.
A waiter says: 'I must ask the person who runs this restaurant if we can give you a discount.'
You tell your friend that you got a raise, because the person who leads your team is happy with your work. Which noun means 'boss' (male)?
It is a sunny day. The children are not in the house, but are playing in the garden.
The restaurant has tables inside and some on the pavement. You prefer to sit in the fresh air.
Your friend asks: 'Where are the kids?' You point through the window: 'They are not in the room, they are ...' Which adverb means 'outside'?
After ten years you meet your old school friends again, and you hug each other in tears of joy.
At the end of a phone call you say a polite word that means you hope to meet or talk again.
The sign on the shop door says: 'Thank you for your visit, goodbye.' Which noun is used in the phrase for 'goodbye'? It also means 'reunion'.
You look in the mirror and point at yourself: 'It is a photo of ...' Which word means 'me' as an object?
Your friend calls your name. You say: 'You can phone ... tomorrow.' Which pronoun means 'me' after a verb?
A child hurts herself and says: 'I washed ...' meaning that she washed herself. Which word means 'me, myself'?
The dentist says: 'Please open wide.' She looks inside the part of your face with your teeth and tongue.
You eat an apple. What part of your face do you use to bite and chew?
A baby is hungry and cries. The mother puts the spoon to its lips. Which noun means 'mouth'?

en: to dress, to get dressed, to put on, to attract, to tighten
situations: It is cold outside. Before you leave the house you take a coat from the hook and put your arms in the sleeves.
In the morning you help your small daughter to put her shirt and trousers on.
A magnet pulls small nails towards it, and a good film pulls viewers. Which verb can mean 'to dress', 'to put on' or 'to attract'?
Your neighbours play music so strongly that you cannot sleep. How would you describe the music?
A child screams in the playground and everyone covers their ears.
The opposite of quiet: the traffic on the main road is full of noise. Which adjective means 'loud'?
The shortest month of the year comes after January and before March. Sometimes it has 29 days.
Carnival and Valentine's Day take place in this winter month.
On a calendar the second page shows this month. Which noun means 'February'?
Your phone rings at 8 p.m. It is your mother and she wants to talk.
The secretary says to the boss: 'There was someone on the line for you while you were in the meeting.'
You missed a notice on your screen showing that someone tried to reach you. Which noun means 'phone call'?

en: to buy, to purchase, to shop
situations: In the supermarket you put milk, bread and cheese on the belt and give the cashier money.
You see a nice jacket in a shop window. You go in, try it on and take it home after you hand over your card.
Your friend says: 'I want to get a new phone because mine is broken.' Which verb means 'to buy'?
You look out of the window and see clouds and rain. Then you check the forecast on your phone.
The newsreader says: 'Tomorrow it will be sunny with 25 degrees in the south.'
Your friend asks if you want to go on a picnic. You say it depends on whether it rains or the sun shines. Which noun means 'weather'?
You travel to Berlin for three days. You book a place where you sleep in a room and have breakfast, and pay for each night.
A tourist asks the taxi driver to take him to the building with a lobby and a front desk where his room is booked.
For your holiday you choose between a flat and a building with many rooms and staff. Which noun means 'hotel'?
You slice a round red vegetable for your salad. It has many small seeds inside.
Your mother makes a sauce for the pasta with red fruits from the garden and some basil.
On a pizza there is cheese and a sauce made from a red fruit. Which noun means 'tomato'?
You cannot find your keys and ask your wife about the place where they are.
You are in a new city and need a pharmacy. You ask a passer-by about its position.
Your friend says he has moved. You ask about the place he lives in now. Which word means 'where'?
You are invited to a dinner and your host asks you to carry a bottle of wine and a dessert with you.
Your sister is coming back from Italy and says she will have a gift for you in her suitcase.
The teacher says: 'Tomorrow, please come with your dictionary.' Which verb means 'to bring along'?
You wear a suit to a funeral. It is the colour of coal and the night sky.
A cat sits in the dark and you can barely see it, because it is the opposite colour of white.
At the cafe you order a drink with no milk, the colour of ink. Which adjective means 'black'?
On a form it asks what you do for fun in your free time. You write: painting and playing guitar.
A new colleague asks you what you like to do after work. You say that you love collecting stamps.
Which noun, borrowed from English, means 'hobby'?
You look in the newspaper and find a small text with a picture that offers a flat for rent.
On the website there is a banner that tries to sell you shoes while you read the news.
A screen at the station shows when the next train comes. Which noun can mean 'advertisement' or 'display'?
At the petrol station you put fifty of these into your car. Fuel is sold by this measure of volume.
A bottle of water at the supermarket contains 1,000 millilitres. Which unit is that?
A recipe asks for half a unit of milk, that is 500 ml. Which noun means 'litre'?

en: to press, to push, to squeeze, to hug
situations: The door does not open when you pull it. You put your hand flat against it and push.
You put your finger on the doorbell button until it rings.
At the airport you meet your old friend and take her in your arms tightly. Which verb means 'to press, push' or 'to hug'?
For a birthday party your aunt bakes something sweet in the oven with flour, eggs and sugar, and cuts it into pieces.
In the cafe you order a piece of something sweet with fruit and cream to eat with your tea.
On Sunday afternoon the family sits together with coffee and a sweet baked dish. Which noun means 'cake'?
The sun goes down, you finish work and come home to have dinner. What part of the day is it?
A friend says: 'Let's meet after dinner, around eight o'clock.' Which noun refers to this time of day?
When you leave the office, it is neither morning nor afternoon, and it is getting dark. Which noun means 'evening'?
A sign in the museum says that visitors must not take photos. You want to explain a general rule that applies to people in general. Which small word means 'one' or 'you' in general?
A friend asks how to get a visa. You say: 'First you fill in a form, then you wait.' You speak about people in general, not about a particular person.
A teacher explains: 'Everybody writes it this way.' Which indefinite pronoun means 'one, you, they'?
On a form there are two boxes for sex: male and the other one. A woman ticks it.
In class the teacher explains the nouns: some are masculine, some neuter, and some are of the gender that goes with women.
A zoo sign tells you that the animal in the cage is a lioness, not a lion. Which adjective means 'female'?
Your train from Munich gets to the station in Berlin at 10 a.m. You step out onto the platform.
After a long drive you phone your mother and say: 'We have got to the hotel safely.'
The flight is delayed. The airport screen shows that the plane has not yet landed. Which verb means 'to arrive'?
A friend asks you about your best-liked song. You say: 'This is my ... song.' Which word, joined to other words, means 'favourite'?
A child shows you the toy he loves most and calls it his ... toy.
At the restaurant the waiter asks about your most-loved dish. Which word placed before a noun means 'favourite'?
The waiter offers you more soup, but you have had enough. You say: 'No, thank you, I do ... want any.'
Your friend asks if you like fish. You make a face and shake your head: 'I do ... like it.'
You say the door is open, but the opposite is true. You make a sentence negative. Which adverb means 'not'?
You go on a long trip and pack your clothes and shoes into a big box with wheels and a handle.
At the airport you wait at the belt for your luggage to come out.
The taxi driver puts your big, heavy luggage in the boot. Which noun means 'suitcase'?
You take a round red or green fruit from the bowl and bite into it. It keeps the doctor away, as they say.
For a snack your mother cuts a crunchy fruit into slices and gives them to you.
At the market you buy a kilo of round fruits that grow on trees, are red or green and make juice. Which noun means 'apple'?
It is midnight. You turn off the light, close your eyes and rest in your bed until morning.
The baby is quiet in the cradle and does not move. Everyone speaks softly.
A friend yawns and says: 'I have not rested enough for three days.' Which verb means 'to sleep'?
You feel hot and cold at the same time. The thermometer shows 39 degrees and the doctor says that your body temperature is too high.
Your child is sick and her forehead is very warm. The nurse measures it with a thermometer.
The doctor says: 'You must stay in bed. Your temperature is high.' Which noun means 'fever'?
In the park a tall plant with a thick trunk, branches and green leaves gives shade.
In autumn the leaves of the big plants fall to the ground and children rake them.
A squirrel climbs up a trunk with branches and leaves. Which noun means 'tree'?
In the market you find a shirt for only 5 euros. It does not cost much.
You compare two phones: one costs 800 euros and the other only 100. The second one does not cost a lot.
The opposite of expensive: a friend says: 'I found a hotel that doesn't cost much.' Which adjective means 'cheap'?
The leaves turn red and yellow, and the tenth month begins after September.
The big beer festival in Munich ends in the first days of this month.
On a calendar the tenth page shows this month. Which noun means 'October'?

en: to come with, to come too, to come along, to keep up
situations: Your friends are going to the cinema. They say: 'Do you want to join us?' You say yes.
You go for a walk fast and your friend cannot go as quickly, so you wait. She asks you to slow down so she can follow your pace.
A colleague asks: 'Are you going to the party tonight?' You say: 'I will go with you.' Which verb means 'to come along'?
On Friday you go to the cinema with your friends and watch a story on a big screen.
Your favourite actor stars in a new picture. You buy popcorn and sit in the dark room.
At home you choose something to watch on a streaming service with a story and actors. Which noun means 'film, movie'?
On a hot summer day you go swimming in a big body of fresh water surrounded by land.
In the mountains there is a big clear body of water in a valley, with boats and a beach.
Your family has a picnic at the water's edge and the children jump in. It is not a river or the sea. Which noun means 'lake'?
Your friend asks: 'Tea or coffee?' You answer that you would prefer tea. Which adverb shows what you prefer?
The waiter asks: 'Fish or meat?' You say you like fish more. Which word means 'rather'?
You say: 'I would prefer to stay at home tonight than go out.' Which adverb means 'rather'?
You tell the receptionist the digits on your room key: 305. What are these digits together?
Somebody asks you to write down your phone digits on a piece of paper.
A runner wears a sign with 42 on her shirt for the race. Which noun means 'number'?
On Saturday you take a bag and go to the supermarket to get food for the week.
Your mother writes a list with milk, bread and eggs, and sends you to the shops.
Before Christmas the town centre is full of people who are buying presents. Which verb means 'to shop'?
It is the hottest month. School is out and many people go on holiday. It comes after July.
The eighth month of the year has 31 days and is often sunny.
On a calendar the eighth page shows this month. Which noun means 'August'?
The library is silent and you can concentrate. How would you describe it?
The baby is not crying, and everyone is relaxed. The street where you live has hardly any traffic and no noise.
Your friend is not nervous before the exam and sits there with a smile. Which adjective means 'calm, quiet'?
On the train a voice says: 'The next stop is Cologne.' What is it called?
At the airport a loudspeaker says that the flight to Rome is delayed.
At the supermarket the loudspeaker says: 'Attention please, the shop closes in ten minutes.' Which noun means 'announcement'?
You talk about yourself and point at your chest. Which word do you use for 'I'?
The teacher asks: 'Who has done the homework?' You raise your hand and say: '... have!' Which pronoun means 'I'?
A friend asks who wants some cake. You say you do. Which word means 'I'?
At lunchtime you sit down with a plate of rice and chicken and use your fork.
The whole family sits around the table and takes the food in their mouths with spoons.
A friend says: 'I am hungry. Let's put something in our stomachs.' Which verb means 'to eat'?
It is cold, there is snow in many places, and the year ends. Christmas comes in this month.
It is the twelfth and last month of the year. People get ready for New Year's Eve.
On a calendar the last page shows this month. Which noun means 'December'?
Before you start eating, the waiter says: 'Enjoy your meal.' You feel the wish to eat and your stomach rumbles.
You are sick and don't want to eat anything. The doctor asks if you have a desire for food.
Your mother cooks soup and says: 'I hope you are hungry!' Which noun means 'appetite'?
Your train is late, so you miss the second train that you wanted to take to the next city.
You plug a cable into the little hole on the back of the computer to connect the printer.
At the airport the sign says: 'Flight changes: your onward flight leaves from gate B.' Which noun means 'connection'?
You meet a man at a party and your friend says: 'Oh, I have met him before.' What does your friend do?
A tourist asks you about a restaurant. You say: 'Yes, I have been there many times, I am familiar with it.'
A teacher asks if you have heard of the writer Goethe. You say you are acquainted with his work. Which verb means 'to know' (a person or a place)?

en: just, now, just now, right now
situations: The phone rings while you are cooking. You say: 'Sorry, I am busy at this very moment.'
A friend asks: 'Where is Anna?' You answer: 'She left a minute ago.' Which adverb means 'just now'?
You look up from the book and say that you are reading at this very second. Which adverb means 'right now'?
The teacher gives an exercise that every student can solve in one minute. It is not hard.
A recipe has only three steps and few ingredients. How would you describe it?
The instructions for the new phone are clear and easy to follow. Which adjective means 'simple, easy'?
At the beginning of every month you transfer money to the owner of your flat.
Your landlord says that from next year the sum you pay each month for the flat will go up.
A friend says: 'My flat is nice but the monthly cost for living there is too high.' Which noun means 'rent'?
The bus comes every fifteen minutes. How long do you wait at most?
You say to your friend: 'Wait for me, I will be ready in 15 minutes.'
The doctor says: 'You must wait for the result.' It takes 15 minutes. Which noun means 'quarter of an hour'?
The soup is boring and has no taste. You take a white powder from a small shaker and put some on.
You cook pasta and the recipe says to put a spoonful of the white crystals in the water.
At the table you ask your neighbour to pass the shaker next to the pepper. Which noun means 'salt'?
Your cousin and his girlfriend are going to the registry office next month and will become husband and wife.
A friend shows you her ring and says: 'We have decided that we will be husband and wife in June.'
A man asks his girlfriend to be his wife for life. Which verb means 'to get married'?
You learn German at an evening school. It is a means of speaking and writing which people of one country use.
In Switzerland people speak German, French and Italian. What are these three?
A friend says: 'I speak three of them: Bengali, English and a little German.' Which noun means 'language'?
At the side of the road there is a board with a red circle and a number: 30. You must drive slowly.
On the door of the office a plate says the name of the doctor.
A board in the park shows a picture of a dog with a red line through it. Which noun means 'sign'?
In spring the grass and the leaves on the trees have this colour.
At the traffic light you can go when the light shows this colour.
You mix blue and yellow and get a new colour, like a frog. Which adjective means 'green'?
In the evening you sit on the sofa and look at the pages of a novel and follow the words with your eyes.
At the breakfast table your father looks at the newspaper and takes in the news.
The teacher says: 'Please say the text aloud from the book.' Which verb means 'to read'?
The floor is wet and a yellow sign warns people not to slip. The sign says to be careful.
The mother tells the child at the road: 'Be careful, there are cars!' Which noun is the warning?
At work, a box says: 'Handle with care. Glass.' Which noun means 'caution'?
You have breakfast at 7 a.m. nearly every day, but on Sundays you sleep late. What is your usual habit?
A friend asks if you take the bus. You say: 'In most cases, yes, apart from when it rains and I take a taxi.'
A colleague says: 'On most days, I work from home.' Which adverb means 'mostly'?
A student works for three months in a company to learn what the job is like, but is not paid much.
Before you finish your studies, the university requires that you gain some experience at a firm.
A young person says: 'Next summer I will do a short period of work to learn the job in a hospital.' Which noun means 'internship'?
You see your friend's umbrella and ask: 'Is this ... umbrella?' Which word means 'your' (informal)?
You talk to your brother: 'Where is ... phone?' Which possessive means 'your' for a friend or family?
You tell a classmate: 'I like ... idea.' Which informal word means 'your'?
On Friday evening you finish work, and you have two days without school or the office: Saturday and Sunday.
You ask your friend: 'What are you doing on Saturday and Sunday?'
The shops are closed on Sundays, so you do your shopping before the days off begin. Which noun means 'weekend'?
You move the mouse to the button on the screen and press it with your finger to open the page.
The teacher says: 'Go to the website and then use the left mouse button on the link.'
On the webshop you choose the shoes and then press the 'buy' button with your mouse. Which verb means 'to click'?
Tomorrow you must sit at a desk for two hours and answer questions to get your certificate. You are nervous.
A mechanic looks at your car to see if it is safe to drive, and it passes.
At the end of the course you write a big test with a grade. Which noun means 'exam'?
You go for a walk in the rain, but you forgot to put on the things that protect your feet. They are wet.
In a shop you try on a leather item for your foot, size 42, and walk around.
At the door of the flat, people take off the things on their feet and leave them on a rack. Which noun means 'shoe'?
You have a holiday at the beach, the sun is shining and the food is delicious. You tell your friend that it is fantastic.
Your friend plays the violin and everyone in the room is amazed at how beautiful the music is.
A colleague asks: 'How was the concert?' You say it was extremely good, better than great. Which adjective means 'wonderful'?
For your friend's birthday you buy a book and wrap it in colourful paper with a bow.
At Christmas there are many wrapped boxes under the tree for everyone in the family.
You are invited to a party. You bring a small gift for the host. Which noun means 'gift, present'?

en: to live, to dwell, to reside
situations: You rent a flat on the third floor of a building in Berlin and sleep there every night. Where do you stay?
A friend asks: 'Do you have your own place, or do you stay with your parents?'
A new colleague asks you in which city you have your home. Which verb means 'to live' (in a place)?
At the travel agency you take a colourful folded paper with pictures and prices of hotels in Spain.
A shop puts printed pages in your mailbox with this week's special offers.
At the tourist office you pick up a small printed booklet with information about the town. Which noun means 'brochure, leaflet'?
At the station you wait on the platform for a long vehicle on rails that takes you from Hamburg to Munich.
The conductor checks your ticket in the long line of carriages that moves on tracks.
Instead of flying you decide to travel by a vehicle that runs on rails and stops at many stations. Which noun means 'train'?
Your friend asks: 'Will you come to the party?' You are not sure, there is a chance, but you have not decided.
A colleague asks if it will rain tomorrow. You say that it is possible, but you do not know for certain.
You are not certain about your answer and say: 'It is possible.' Which adverb means 'maybe'?

en: to lie, to be located, to be situated
situations: You are tired and rest flat on the sofa with your legs stretched out.
A book is on the table. It is not standing, it is flat on the surface.
A tourist asks you: 'Where is Hamburg?' You say it is in the north of the country. Which verb means 'to lie' or 'to be situated'?
At the station a sign shows that the train to Cologne leaves at 10:15. What does the board show?
You are late and run to the bus. The driver closes the doors and the bus is already moving away.
The timetable has two columns: arrival and the time when the vehicle goes. Which noun means 'departure'?
You wait for the train at the station on a raised area beside the tracks, at number 4.
The announcement says: 'The train to Munich arrives at number 7.' Where do you stand?
A woman asks you: 'Where do I wait for my train?' You point to the long strip of ground beside the rails. Which noun means 'platform' (at a station)?
You have a cold, a fever and a cough, so you stay in bed and do not go to work.
Your child cannot go to school today because she does not feel well and has a high temperature.
The opposite of healthy: your colleague is not at the office. Which adjective means 'sick, ill'?
You travel alone on business and book a room in a hotel for one person with one bed.
At the reception the clerk asks: 'For how many persons?' You say: 'Only for me.' What kind of room do you want?
A couple needs a double room, but you are travelling alone. Which noun means 'single room'?

en: to help, to aid, to assist
situations: Your neighbour carries heavy boxes up the stairs. You take one end and give a hand.
A child cannot tie his shoes. His mother ties them for him so that he can walk.
A tourist is lost. You show him the way. Which verb means 'to help'?
In the laundry room you put your clothes into a big device with a round door that washes them.
At the factory a large device with moving parts makes thousands of bottles every day.
The coffee device in the office is broken. Which noun means 'machine'?
You open a drawing of the city on your phone to find the way to the museum.
Before your holiday you write a list of what you will do each day, so that everything is organised.
At the train station there is a timetable with all the trains. Which noun can mean 'plan', 'map' or 'schedule'?
In a shop you hold two jackets and ask your friend to choose: 'The red or the blue? ... one do you like?' Which word means 'which'?
A waiter holds two cakes and asks you to pick one. You ask him about the options. Which question word means 'which'?
You point at three bags on a shelf and ask the seller about the one you should buy. Which word means 'which'?
At the end of the dinner the waiter brings a paper with the total amount you must pay.
At the end of the month the electricity company sends you a letter with the amount you owe for the power.
A teacher writes: 3 + 4 = 7 and says the working out is correct. Which noun can mean 'bill' or 'calculation'?

en: to play, to gamble, to act, to perform
situations: The children run in the garden and play with a ball and toys.
At the weekend you and your friends take out the guitar and make music.
In the evening the family sits around the table with cards and has fun. Which verb means 'to play'?
A woman has no boss and runs her own small shop. She works for herself.
A teenager moves out of the house and washes, cooks and pays for everything without his parents' help.
On a form for your job there is a box if you work for yourself or for a company. Which adjective means 'independent'?
At the table you say: 'Could I have a larger amount of rice, please?' Which word means 'more'?
You have two euros, but you need five. You say: 'I need a greater amount of money.'
The teacher says: 'You have to practise a greater amount if you want to improve.' Which adverb means 'more'?
The thermometer shows 25, which is warm. What is the unit for temperature?
The weather forecast says: 'Tomorrow it will be minus two.' Which unit does the forecaster use?
A teacher draws a circle on the board and says it has 360 of them. Which noun means 'degree'?
The teacher writes on the board: 'I go to school.' It starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.
A student writes an essay and uses many short groups of words with a verb and a subject.
Your homework asks you to make a complete line with the new word. Which noun means 'sentence'?

en: to take, to have, to use
situations: The waiter asks what you would like. You say: 'I will choose the soup.'
You reach out and pick up a piece of cake from the plate.
A friend asks: 'How will you get to the airport?' You say you will use the bus. Which verb means 'to take'?
You do not take the bus to work, but drive on four wheels with your own engine and steering wheel.
At the petrol station you fill up your vehicle and then clean the windows.
Your father buys a new vehicle for the family. It is blue and has five doors. Which noun means 'car'?
In your flat the room with a cooker, a fridge and a sink is where you prepare your meals.
A restaurant is famous for its Italian style of cooking. Which noun means this way of cooking?
Your mother is cooking in the room next to the living room. Which noun means 'kitchen'?

en: seller, vendor, shop assistant, salesperson, salesman
situations: In the shoe shop a man in a uniform asks if you need help and brings you a pair in your size.
At the market a man stands behind a table full of fruit and shouts the prices.
You ask a man in the electronics shop about the best laptop for you. Which noun means 'salesman, shop assistant' (male)?
It is midnight, you have worked all day and your eyes keep closing. You can hardly wait to get into bed.
A baby yawns and rubs her eyes after a long afternoon of playing. How does she feel?
At the end of a long journey your friend says that he has no energy left and needs rest. Which adjective means 'tired'?
You sit on a plane and look down at the clouds as it moves through the air at 10,000 metres.
A bird opens its wings and rises into the sky above the trees.
You go from Berlin to Rome in two hours, not by train or by car. Which verb means 'to fly'?
A clock goes round twice, which makes twenty-four hours. What is this period of time called?
Between sunrise and sunset it is light outside. What do you call this time, the opposite of night?
Monday is the first one of the week. Which noun means 'day'?
Early in the morning you walk to a small shop and buy fresh bread rolls and a loaf for breakfast.
A shop smells of warm bread and cakes. A woman behind the counter puts rolls into a paper bag.
You need bread for dinner and your friend says: 'Go to the shop on the corner where they bake it.' Which noun means 'bakery'?

en: very (much), really, a lot, highly, greatly, extremely
situations: The soup is extremely hot, so you wait before you eat it. Which small word makes the adjective stronger?
A friend gives you a present and you say: 'Thank you so much, I like it a lot.'
The film was not just good, it was to a high degree good. Which adverb means 'very'?
You do not write a letter on paper. You type a message on your computer and send it to your boss's address with an @ sign.
The teacher asks for your electronic address so she can send you the homework.
On the form there is a line for your address with an @ in it. Which noun means 'email'?
At the party the music starts and you move your body to the rhythm with your friends on the floor.
At a wedding the bride and groom open the floor and move together to a slow song.
At a club your friend says: 'Let's go and move to the music!' Which verb means 'to dance'?
Your father works for a business with a hundred employees that makes cars.
A sign on the building shows the name of the organisation that sells computers and has an office on the third floor.
At an interview the boss asks: 'Why do you want to work for our organisation?' Which noun means 'company'?
You hand a friend a present and say: 'This is for ...' Which informal word means 'to you'?
You ask a friend: 'Can I give ... a lift to the station?' Which word means 'you' (informal, after 'to')?
A child's mother says: 'Do you feel better? How is it going for ... ?' Which informal pronoun means 'you'?
In an apartment building you live on the third level above the ground floor. Which noun do you use for a level of a building?
An old man walks slowly in the park and leans on a long piece of wood in his hand.
In the lift there are buttons for each level of the building. Which noun can mean 'floor' (of a building) or 'stick'?
The water in the lake is so clean that you can see the bottom. How is the water?
The teacher explains the task and everyone says that they understand it very well. Nothing is confusing.
After a rainy day the sky has no clouds at all. Which adjective means 'clear'?

en: to stop, to cease, to end
situations: The rain has been falling all day. At six o'clock it finally does not fall any more.
The teacher says: 'Please do not talk any more, the lesson has begun.' What should the students do?
Your doctor says you should not smoke any more. You give it up. Which verb means 'to stop, to cease'?
A man stays at home while his wife goes to work. He cooks, cleans and takes the children to school.
On a form for a man there is the job: he takes care of the home and the children.
Your neighbour says: 'My husband does not have a job outside, he runs our home.' Which noun means 'house husband'?
You rent a small home in a big building in the city, with one room, a kitchen and a bathroom.
A friend from America says that he lives in a small home on the sixth floor of a tower.
A website shows modern homes for rent in the city centre. Which noun, borrowed from English, means 'apartment'?
At the hairdresser's you ask her to cut your locks, which are growing on your head.
In the shower you wash the strands that grow on your head with shampoo.
A friend says: 'You have a thin line growing on your jacket from your cat.' Which noun means 'hair' (a single one)?
You pick up your phone, type your friend's number and wait until she answers.
The boss says to the secretary: 'Please ring the customer and tell him that the delivery is late.'
You want to reserve a table. You take your phone and dial the number of the restaurant. Which verb means 'to call, to phone'?
A friend says: 'I am going away on holiday.' You ask about the destination of the trip.
You see your colleague with a suitcase and ask him about the place he is going to.
At the station a tourist asks you about the direction of your journey. Which question word means 'where to'?
A man from Hamburg has a passport from Germany. How do you call him?
At the border the officer asks a man for his passport. The man says that he is from Munich. Which noun describes his nationality?
At a conference people from many countries meet. A man from Berlin introduces himself. Which noun means 'German' (male person)?
A girl and you spend a lot of time together, you share secrets and laugh together. She is not your sister.
A man says: 'Tonight I will take the woman I am in love with to dinner.'
A woman says about the person she has known since school: 'We tell each other everything.' Which noun means 'friend' or 'girlfriend' (female)?
You have bought a phone today, so it is not old and has never been used before.
You start your first day in a different job and meet colleagues you have not met yet.
The opposite of old: your friend wears a coat that she bought yesterday. Which adjective means 'new'?
A man points to the little girl next to him and says that she is the female child of him and his wife.
At the parents' evening the teacher talks to a mother about her female child, who is eight years old.
You have one son and one girl. Which noun means 'daughter'?

en: to spend the night, to stay overnight
situations: You travel far and sleep in a hostel for one night before you continue the next morning.
Your friend lives in another city. You stay at her flat for the night, because the last train has gone.
A hotel sign says: 'Overnight stays from 50 euros.' Which verb means 'to spend the night'?
An old man with white hair plays chess with a child. He is the father of the child's mother.
A boy says: 'My dad's dad lives in a small village and has a big garden.'
At the family dinner the oldest man at the table is the father of your father. Which noun means 'grandfather'?
You call the dentist's office and get a fixed time, Tuesday at 3 p.m., for your check-up.
Your boss asks you to write a note in your calendar for the meeting with the customer on Friday.
The project must be handed in by the end of the month. Which noun can mean 'appointment' or 'deadline'?
You fall off your bike and shout so that someone will come and assist you.
The old woman cannot carry her bags and says: 'Thank you for your hand.'
You carry a heavy sofa and ask your neighbour for support. Which noun means 'help'?
You have two brothers and one sister. How would you say that these people are part of your family?
At the till the clerk asks if you possess a loyalty card. You say that you do.
A friend says: 'I am hungry because I do not possess any food at home.' Which verb means 'to have'?
The doctor looks at your test results and says that nothing is unusual.
Your friend asks if the strange noise from the car is a problem. The mechanic says that this is the usual sound.
The teacher says: 'Today is an ordinary day, there is no test.' Which adjective means 'normal'?
On the main street you walk past a place where you can buy clothes, shoes and gifts.
Your uncle runs a place that sells furniture. He opens it every morning at nine.
A company signs an important agreement with another company about buying and selling. Which noun can mean 'shop' or 'business deal'?
You point at a chair in the corner and say: 'The keys are on the chair, they are ...' Which adverb means 'there'?
Your friend asks: 'Are you at home?' You answer: 'Yes, I am present.' Which short word means 'here, there'?
A child looks into a box and says: 'Look, it is ...!' Which adverb means 'there'?
You speak about your neighbours: 'I gave the book to ...' Which word means 'to them'?
Your friends are lost and call you. You say: 'I will show the way to ...' Which pronoun means 'to them'?
You tell a story about the children: 'My mother gave sweets to ...' Which word means 'them'?
In many cities a long vehicle with wires above runs on rails in the middle of the street and stops at stops.
You take an electric vehicle in the street that goes on tracks, not underground, and costs less than a taxi.
In Berlin, Vienna and Prague you can see yellow or red vehicles on rails in the road. Which noun means 'tram'?
A man stands outside the office and lights a cigarette. Smoke comes out of his mouth.
The sign in the restaurant says that you are not allowed to do this inside, where the air must stay clean.
The doctor says that you should not do what puts tobacco smoke in your lungs. Which verb means 'to smoke'?
You rent a flat. Each month you send the money to the man who owns the building.
The heating is broken. You call the man who owns the house and ask him to send a plumber.
A tenant says: 'The man who let me this flat is very friendly.' Which noun means 'landlord'?
On a compass the needle points to the top of the map. Which direction is this?
You live in Munich and your friend lives in Hamburg, a long way up the map. In which direction is Hamburg?
A weather forecaster says: 'It will be cold in the upper part of the country.' Which noun means 'north'?
A man from Italy and a man from Poland meet. They both come from the same continent.
At the airport there are two lines: one for people with passports from the EU countries, and one for others.
A tourist from Asia says: 'In Paris, Rome and Berlin I met many people from this continent.' Which noun means 'European' (male)?
You ring your friend and for an hour you use your voice to say things on the phone.
The teacher asks: 'Do you want to use German in the conversation, or English?'
At the meeting the manager says words into the microphone for ten minutes. Which verb means 'to speak'?
The sign on the wall shows a cigarette with a red line. It is against the rules to do it here.
At the pool a sign says that you may not jump in from the side. Which adjective describes this action?
The police officer says that parking here is against the law. Which adjective means 'forbidden'?
A young man goes to lectures at the university and writes exams. He is learning to become an engineer.
On the bus a young man shows a card and gets a discount because he studies at the university.
A friend says about his brother: 'He is at university, he studies medicine.' Which noun means 'student' (male)?
At the bottom of the contract there is a line where you must write your name by hand.
The postman gives you a parcel and asks you to put your name on his phone screen.
On the form the clerk says: 'Please write your name here, with your pen, at the end.' Which noun means 'signature'?

en: left, on the left, to the left
situations: You stand at the crossing. To reach the bakery you must turn to the side of your body where your heart is.
A driver says: 'Take the next turn on the side that is not the right one.'
The taxi driver asks: 'Right or ... ?' Which adverb means 'left'?
At the supermarket you put your shopping on a belt and then pay the person who scans it.
At the cinema you queue in front of the window where you buy a ticket.
At the end of your shopping trip you queue at the place where everyone pays. Which noun means 'checkout, till'?

en: to board, to get on, to get in
situations: The bus stops at the stop and you step through the door to take your seat.
The taxi arrives. You open the door and sit inside.
The announcement says: 'The train to Hamburg is ready, please go aboard.' Which verb means 'to board, to get on'?
You sit at your desk and type a report on a machine with a screen and a keyboard.
At school the children learn how to write a program on a machine in the classroom.
A friend says: 'My laptop is broken, and I need a new one.' Which noun, borrowed from English, means 'computer'?
You have a headache and a fever. You make an appointment with a woman in a white coat who examines you.
A friend says: 'My aunt works at the hospital and treats sick people.' Which word is used for a female medical person like her?
Your child is sick and you call a woman who can treat her. Which noun means 'doctor' (female)?
A child breaks a plate and her father's face turns red. He shouts. How does he feel?
In the fairy tale the witch wants to harm the princess. What kind of person is the witch?
Your neighbour is upset because someone parked in front of her garage. Which adjective can mean 'angry' or 'evil'?
You open your mouth and tell your friend the news that you got a new job.
A child asks: 'What did the teacher tell you yesterday?' You repeat the words.
The boss wants to know the reason. You give him your answer in words. Which verb means 'to say'?
The sun is at its highest point and the clock shows twelve. What time of day is it?
The school canteen opens at twelve and the children go to eat their main meal.
A shop sign says: 'Closed from 12 to 2.' Which noun means 'noon, midday'?
Every morning a man in a yellow uniform brings letters and parcels to your door.
You must send a parcel to your brother in another country, so you go to a building with counters and stamps.
You put a stamp on a card and drop it into the yellow box. Which noun means 'mail' or 'post office'?
You look in the fridge and there is not a single thing to eat. Which word describes what you find?
The teacher asks: 'What did you learn today?' You are embarrassed and say that you learned zero things. Which pronoun is that?
A friend asks what is in the box. You open it and it is empty. Which word means 'nothing'?
At the entrance of the museum you pay and the clerk gives you a small piece of paper that lets you go in.
You are going to a concert. At the box office you buy a paper that you must show at the door.
You want to go to the zoo. Which noun means the 'ticket' for entering a place, not for a train?
You put your old bike on the internet. A man pays you 100 euros and rides away on it.
A baker stands behind the counter and gives bread to customers in return for money.
You do not need your old phone any more and give it to someone who pays you for it. Which verb means 'to sell'?
The teacher writes 'house' on the board and asks you to say it in another language. What did she write?
A sentence is made up of many small units. You do not know the meaning of one of them, so you look it up in the dictionary.
You learn new vocabulary every day. Which noun means 'word'?
A man asks you for the way to the station. You say: 'Go along this street and don't turn left or right.'
The satnav says to keep going in the same direction for two kilometres.
At the traffic light a tourist asks: 'Do I turn here?' You say: 'No, keep going forward.' Which adverb means 'straight ahead'?
A thief takes your bag. You dial 110 and officers in uniform arrive at the scene.
After a car accident, a man in a blue uniform writes down what happened.
A child is lost in the town. The mother asks officers in a car with blue lights for help. Which noun means 'police'?
You and your friend buy the same shirt in the same colour and size. They look just alike.
In class all students get the same task, and nobody gets a different one.
Two plus two and one plus three give the same result. Which adjective means 'same, equal'?
Before your trip to Italy you buy a book with maps, tips and information about hotels and sights.
A tourist walks around Rome with a thick book in his hand and reads about the history of each building.
At the bookshop you ask for a book that gives advice for visitors to Spain. Which noun means 'guidebook'?

en: to bathe, to bath, to swim
situations: It is Saturday evening. You fill the tub with hot water and lie in it to relax.
On a hot day at the beach you go into the sea to cool down.
You wash your little baby in a small plastic tub with warm water. Which verb means 'to bathe'?
For breakfast you pour a white liquid from a bottle into your cereal. It comes from cows.
A baby is hungry and her mother gives her a bottle of a white drink.
At the supermarket you buy a carton from the fridge section. It is white and you pour it into your tea. Which noun means 'milk'?
